1601.body:
## Summary

Implements the **startup batch** of `tmp/hive-trustworthiness-development-plan-2026-11-14.md` on top of
`hive/hive3-integration`, and — the point of an earlier revision's gap — puts the diagnostic emitters
into the real Hive owners instead of only modeling events in tests.

Branch is up to date with `hive/hive3-integration` at `faf4aaab` (merged in `cf95113e`, the third base
merge; the earlier merges were `f22ad404` and `780c7402`).

### What is implemented

- `temp/hive-trust/src/dm_hive_trust/diagnostics/events.py` — correlated, token-validated events; no
  free-text field, so prompt/tool/reply text can never be copied in; explicit `AUTHORITATIVE` /
  `OBSERVATION` / `CLIENT_DISPLAY` evidence kinds.
- `.../query.py` — conservative "where did this request stop?" investigation: it names the last proven
  stage, the stage being waited on, the missing evidence and the next owner. It never fetches state,
  retries, or guesses a root cause.
- `.../recording.py` — `DiagnosticRecorder`, `DiagnosticReceiver`, `scope_token`, `LogSink`. Passive by
  construction: an unsafe identifier is dropped rather than raised, a failing sink is contained, and
  correlation is a context variable so concurrent turns cannot cross-attribute events.
- `.../settings.py` — the single, explicit deployment switch:
  `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_DIAGNOSTICS=log` installs a `LogSink` recorder; absent/`off` installs none;
  any other value raises instead of silently disabling evidence.
- Real emitters at the owner boundaries named in plan §6.2 (see `temp/hive-trust/TRACEABILITY.md`):
  - `server_engine/hive_turn_startup.py` — `message.received`, `admission.result` (AUTHORITATIVE only when
    the Store returned the committed receipt), `beebou.started`, `beebou.result`, `result.committed`,
    `output.attempt`, `output.result`; `DiagnosticReceiver` wraps `AdmissionReceiver` for
    `dispatch.started` / `dispatch.receipt` / `dispatch.result`.
  - `server_engine/hive_beebou_model.py` — `model.started` / `model.result` (always OBSERVATION).
  - `server_engine/hive_beebou_tools.py` — `tool.started` / `tool.result` (tool name and status only,
    never arguments or results).
  - `server_engine/server.py` — assembles `configured_recorder(scope)` into `HiveTurnStartup`.

Evidence rules enforced in code: a start/attempt/transport event never proves execution or acceptance; a
transport cancellation at the deadline is recorded `unknown`, never `accepted`, even though the Store may
have committed; a successful Gateway push is never `CLIENT_DISPLAY`; a still-running or `observed` turn
never emits `result.committed`.

### Review findings addressed (F1–F8)

Each fix is the smallest behavior change that answers the finding, and each has a test that failed on the
previous behavior before the fix (5 genuine RED runs, then green).

| Finding | Disposition | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1 an inconclusive authoritative `reconcile.result` erased a proven admission | only definitive outcomes (`accepted`/`queued`/`committed` or a failure) move `accepted`; `unknown`/`not_found` neither sets nor erases it | `test_inconclusive_authoritative_reconcile_does_not_erase_proven_admission` |
| F2 a start inside its budget was reported `UNKNOWN` | a configured budget inside its window is `WAITING`; past it, or with no budget, `UNKNOWN` | `test_start_inside_its_budget_waits_instead_of_reporting_an_unknown_outcome`, `test_start_without_a_configured_budget_stays_unknown` |
| F3 a display of an older version completed a newer commit | the commit is located first; a display only completes it when `version`/`task_ref` agree | `test_display_of_an_older_version_does_not_complete_a_newer_commit`, `test_display_of_the_committed_version_completes_it` |
| F4 ids alone merged two authenticated scopes | `investigate_message` / `investigate_delivery` take the caller's `scope_token` and drop facts without that exact token | `test_another_authenticated_scope_cannot_complete_this_request` |
| F5 `beebou.started` was shadowed and named a fact nobody emits | one branch, one missing-fact name from `_START_EVIDENCE` (`decision.result`), identical before and after the budget | `test_beebou_start_names_the_same_missing_decision_before_and_after_its_budget` |
| F6 README claimed real-Store diagnosis facts | T01/D01 rows now state which participant is real and which is a constructed event | `temp/hive-trust/README.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md` |
| F7 no CI registry rows or wheel entry | wheel force-include, `ci-gates.json` `sourcePaths`/`sourcePackages` and the installed-package transition mapping added. **No `enrolled` suite row**: the CI gate collects enrolled suites with `unittest` discovery while this suite is pytest-style (async cases, `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`), so enrolling it would select zero tests. Recorded as a known gate gap, not silently claimed as covered | `tests/server/test_installed_package_proof.py` |
| F8 token validation was described as redaction | docstrings/README narrowed to "bounded tokens, not a redaction guarantee" | `events.py` |

A second review pass after `cf95113e` raised R1–R8; six were fixed in `d5d338e4` (each test-first), one
was already recorded, and one is the same F7 gate gap. The per-finding table is in the comment
[here](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/DigitalMate/pull/1601#issuecomment-6909293212) and in
`temp/hive-trust/TRACEABILITY.md`.

### Merge resolution notes (base `780c7402`)

The merge keeps both sides rather than dropping either behavior:

- `hive_turn_startup.py`: the base's richer `accept()` (authenticated home ref, queue/addressed
  envelopes, `_HomeInputAdmission`, fresh-submission gate) now also records the Gateway observation,
  wraps the admission receiver with the diagnostic observer and records the Store's own admission;
  `run_input` keeps the base's queued/routed branches inside the diagnostic turn scope.
- `hive_beebou_tools.py`: the base's addressed dispatch and per-turn capacity latches plus the optional
  observer; an addressed call now also reports `tool.result` instead of returning past the observation.
- `server.py`: the base's `operator_api_base` / `require_fresh_submission_id` wiring plus the opt-in
  recorder.
- `temp/hive-beebou/ownership.json`: `bridge` allowed alongside `hive-session-target` and
  `hive-trust-diagnostics`.

### Honest coverage

`T01` (lost admission ACK against the real Store) and `D01–D05` are PASS. `T03` is partial.

**`T02`, `T04–T80`, `C01–C24` and `H01–H08` are NOT_RUN** — they need producers, devices, real models or
Host grants this PR does not provide. Plan §6.2 rows 2 (Inbox/Store enqueue+claim), 5 (Bee
activation/run/state), 8 (recovery) and `decision.result` / `quick_reply.result` / `interaction.state`
are **not instrumented**, because they live in protected owners or need the `telethon`-backed scenario
harness. The full matrix with per-row reasons is in `temp/hive-trust/TRACEABILITY.md`; it must not be
read as a coverage claim for those scenarios.

## Verification

Executed locally in an isolated worktree, Windows, Python 3.13, on head `d5d338e4` (base `faf4aaab`
merged in `cf95113e`):

```text
PYTHONUTF8=1 PYTHONPATH="<test deps>;vendor/mandate-...whl;<every temp/*/src>;harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/src;tests/scenarios" \
E:/miniforge3/envs/py3.13/python.exe -m pytest temp/hive-trust/tests -q
```

Result: **52 passed**. The emitters are exercised by tests that drive the real owners (`accept` over a
real `SQLiteSessionRepository`, `HiveBeebouModel.call` with a controlled Gateway, `HiveBeebouTools.call`
with a faulting provider, `_publish` with failing/succeeding push callables), and the delivery edge cases
run through the real `deliver()` (`StaleReceipt`, `WithheldAcknowledgement`, `SlowStore`).

```text
pytest temp/hive-beebou/tests tests/architecture/test_import_gate.py -q
```

Result: **111 passed, 29 subtests passed** — no regression in the merged Beebou owners, and the AR01/AR02
import gate passes on the real production source.

```text
python -B tools/architecture/transition.py --check docs/implementations/migration/module-ownership.json --root .
```

Result: exit 0; `hive-trust: 2 components, 0 adapters`. `python -m py_compile` on the four touched Bridge
modules → ok.

Packaging: the Bridge wheel force-includes `dm_hive_trust`, `.github/ci-gates.json` and
`scripts/ci/server_context_source.py` list the source package, and `tests/server/test_installed_package_proof.py`
admission/registry tests pass with `hive-trust` registered (**19 passed, 112 subtests, 4 failed, 23
errors**; the 4 failures are `os.symlink` `WinError 1314` privilege tests and the errors are
`InstalledPackageProofTests` bundled-`pip` `ssl.SSLError` in `setUpClass` — both local environment limits).

## Environment limits (not fixed, not claimed)

- `telethon` is not installed, so the Bridge scenario suite around these owners (`TextJourney`,
  `tests/scenarios/hive`) is **BLOCKED** locally, as are the Bridge unit tests that import the scenario
  harness (`test_hive_turn_startup.py`, `test_hive_beebou_*`). No scenario path is reported as verified
  through it.
- `scripts/ci/server-tests.py --suite hive-trust` refuses to run outside the protected trusted runner, so
  the CI gate itself is NOT_RUN locally.
- Symlink-dependent tests fail with `WinError 1314` on this host.
- `InstalledPackageProofTests` bundled `pip` bootstrap fails with `ssl.SSLError`.
- The LF byte pins only match on a checkout without `core.autocrlf` conversion.

No real credentials, accounts, devices, models, databases or external side effects were used. All Store
instances are temporary and synthetic.

## Migration

The partition is read-only and temporary. Move it into the reviewed observability owner once that owner
publishes the event schema and query interface, keep emitters only at the real commit/observation
boundaries, and delete the partition after the owner's tests cover lost ACK, no-reply,
committed-but-undisplayed and unknown-dependency behavior.

SC04-C2 part (a): a Bee session target on `hive.message.send`, implementing design §7a (Phase 3 coordinator, 2026-11-15/16). Part (b), the shared-Home reset refusal, is #1576. G5 covers the **single-device journey**; the two-device part is deferred to v3.5 (§7a at 1164a427).

## Decisions (for §7a)
| # | Decision | Where | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `admission.kind` is `new_task`, `steer_task` or `beebou_turn`. `basis` is the reference field that named the session, as the FIXTURE reference gateway reports it (`target_session_ref`, `reply_to` or `follows`); it is `home_default` only when no reference resolved (no reference, or an unresolved quote). `new_task` / `steer_task` carry `task_id`; a `beebou_turn` carries none (there is no Bee task). *(Amended after review F3: the earlier wording said a referenced send landing on Beebou is `home_default` with a `task_id`, which matched neither the code nor the FIXTURE.)* No client branches on `queue_new_turn` (grep of the ArkTS cloud-adapter, entry and cards on main and hive3; `DigitalMateAdmissionResult` has no `kind`), so no alias is needed. | `hive_turn_startup._admission` | journey, unresolved-quote |
| 2 | A routed message is committed to Beebou's context with **no model call**, as a dispatch tool call `{id, mode, task_ref, text}` plus its tool result, both with `hive_origin="user"` and `hive_routed=true`. The text is byte-equal. | `dm_hive_runtime/assembly/beebou_routed.py` | `test_single_device_journey_across_two_bees` |
| 3 | `[routing] routed_reply` / `routed_steer_reply` / `not_sent_reply` live in the Beebou TOML (`dm_hive_beebou/config/routing.toml`, zh copy). `{bee}` is the Bee's display name, never its `bee_id` or `session_ref`; a Bee with no display name fails the routed turn. A missing or empty template, or one without `{bee}`, fails config load with no fallback. | `dm_hive_beebou.config.settings.load_routing` | `test_missing_or_empty_routed_reply_template_fails_config_load` |
| 4 | The capability name `target_session_ref` is unchanged. | `server.py` (`snapshot_views`) | journey |
| 5 | A target that is foreign, unknown, stale, `EVICTING` or retired returns its refusal, has no effect, and never falls through to another Bee. A `reply_to` that resolves to nothing becomes an ordinary `beebou_turn` with basis `home_default`, no error. | `server_engine/hive_session_target.py` | `test_foreign_stale_and_evicted_targets_never_fall_through`, `test_unresolved_quote_is_an_ordinary_beebou_turn` |

Wire names were adopted by the Phase 3 coordinator on 2026-11-15; the Mobile Gateway, Session Manager and HarmonyOS client owners may reopen them.

## Behaviour
- **Carrier:** `hive.message.send` accepts optional `target_session_ref`, `reply_to` (`{message_id, room_id}`, or the old HAP's `{task_id, part}`), `follows` and `source_ids` (the attachment, as in FIXTURE A02). A send without them behaves exactly as today, with no `admission` key. The `room.message` carrier waits for H-R1 (3.6), so C01 stays BLOCKED.
- **Resolution, before anything is admitted:**
  - `SESSION_TARGET_UNKNOWN`/`not_found`: an unknown or another user's target or `follows`.
  - `SESSION_TARGET_EXPIRED`: `bee_evicted` for a retired or `EVICTING` Bee, `session_ended` for an ended or replaced session.
  - `SESSION_TARGET_CONFLICT`/`target_and_reference_disagree`: references that disagree.
  - Every refusal carries `field`, `reason`, `accepted=false` and `retryable=false`.
- **Routing, keeping the HIVE1 direction rule:** the user's input is a UserInput to Beebou. For a Bee-resolved send, the Host acts for Beebou with no model call:
  - a **SteerTask** of the task the Bee runs now (its Session's RUNNING claim), or of its latest task when that task's state is in `steer_states`;
  - otherwise a **NewTask**.
  - The text goes verbatim through the same BotTools dispatch path, so there is no Store admission change. The routed turn runs through `NativeBeebouRunner` (new `harness_run` hook: Store claim, Host tool plan authorized for that exact call, context commit).
- **Durable route (review F1):** the Bee a send resolves to is written to the Hive Store (`dm_hive_routing_intents`) *before* the input is admitted, and the turn reads it from there. A restart between admission and the turn therefore still routes to the Bee, with no model call and no resend needed. Dispatch planning runs inside the turn's Store claim, so a planning failure (for example a Bee with no display name) is a bounded, recorded turn failure.
- **Admission from the Store (review F2):** every response path builds `admission` from the routing intent plus the `hive-routed-<seq>` plan, including a send whose input the recovery pass ran first.
- **Resends:** a resend of an admitted `message_id` is compared with the recorded intent (none for a Beebou turn).
  - A different destination or text is `SESSION_TARGET_CONFLICT` and changes nothing.
  - The same destination replays the original admission (`status: replayed`), or `pending` while the input has not run.
  - If the routed turn settled as a failure before its dispatch, the same-target retry gets that failure notice (`status: failed`), not a conflict (review F4).
  - Plain resends without references are unchanged.

## Changes
- New `server_engine/hive_session_target.py`, with ownership row `hive-session-target`.
- New `dm_hive_runtime/assembly/beebou_routed.py`.
- New `dm_hive_beebou/config/routing.toml` plus `load_routing`.
- `beebou_native.py`: `harness_run`.
- `hive_turn_startup.py`: params, resolve before admit, routed turn, admission, resend rule, `source_ids`.
- `server.py`: one capability line.
- `engine_errors.py` + en/zh strings: `SESSION_TARGET_*`.
- **Store (disclosed):**
  - read only: `hive_busy.locate_quoted_message`;
  - **new table** `dm_hive_routing_intents` in the Hive Store file, in a new module `server_engine/session_proximity/hive_routing.py` (ownership row `hive-routing-intents`). Writes go through `store_write`; the Hive turn startup creates the table (`HiveRoutingIntents.open`), so the Store owner's `repository.py` and schema list are unchanged. The Session Store owner may want to move it into the repository schema later.

## Evidence (local; CI artifact uploads are quota-blocked)
`test_hive_session_target.py`, 7 tests through the real CLI bridge, WebSocket, Store, Bot Repository and BotTools, with a process restart on the same Store. The model is controlled and only creates the two Bees; the Bee runtime is controlled (`done` plus terminal commit labelled `controlled-host`).
- **Single-device journey across two Bees:**
  - Text to the Report Bee steers its running task, with byte-equal text.
  - An attachment to the Trip Bee becomes a new task carrying `src-invoice`.
  - No model call, and no raw user input to any Bee.
  - The display name appears in the reply; the `bee_id` and `session_ref` do not.
  - The Trip Bee's result lands on its own task, and quoting that result routes back to the Trip Bee.
- **Scoped reset:** `conversation.context.reset` on Home leaves every Bee Session and task unchanged, and the next targeted send still routes.
- **Refusals:** foreign (another user's Session), unknown, `follows`-unknown, conflicting, stale, `EVICTING` and retired targets. Each has no effect.
- **Unresolved quotes** become `beebou_turn`/`home_default`.
- **Plain sends** are unchanged.
- **Conflicting retry after restart:** a new process on the same Store refuses another target and a dropped target, and replays the original admission (same `task_id`, no second dispatch, no model call).
- **Config:** a missing, empty or `{bee}`-less template fails to load.
- **Review fixes** (4 tests, each failing on `59ccc8aa`):
  - `test_restart_before_the_routed_turn_still_routes_to_the_bee` (F1): no resend; the new process's recovery pass routes the input to the Bee.
  - `test_recovery_pass_first_still_reports_the_admission` (F2).
  - `test_same_target_retry_of_a_turn_that_failed_before_dispatch_gets_the_failure` (F4).
  - `test_unhashable_source_ids_are_bad_params` (F5).

Other suites:
- Bridge `test_hive_*` / `test_session_proximity_hive_*`, `temp/hive-runtime/tests`, `temp/hive-beebou/tests` at `6d21dc01`: 280 passed, 2 skipped, 7 xfailed (the 4 `test_engine_errors` failures are pre-existing on main).
- `tests/scenarios/hive` at `6d21dc01`: 224 passed, 21 skipped.
- `tools/architecture/check.py`: 0 findings.

## hive3 composition (not in this PR)
`claude/hive3-sc04-c2a-compose` at `fab64893`, cut from hive3 `ebb04d51`:
- #1297's reference Gateway and cases move to the new kinds. B08 becomes an ordinary Beebou turn, guarded by a new mutant `refuse_unresolved_quote`.
- Adopted codes are marked in `pending-confirmation.json`.
- `gateway_bee_session` is published, and the SC04-C1/C2 owner tests are added.
- Checks there: fixture unittest 32/32, node 13/13.

1604.body:
> **Lands via `hive/hive3-integration`; do not merge to main directly.** Built on `hive/hive3-integration` @ `66fd6c4b`.

Refs #1243 (SC02-C2 G5 condition), #1533. Queue/preempt executor follow-up: #1597.

## Problem

The real Gateway had no entry for the client's busy-time controls (H-C8). Only `hive.bee.stop` took an operation ID. `EngineRequest` refused `session.steer`, `session.queue`, `session.preempt`, `interaction.answer` and `operation.get`, so SC02-C2 and SC02-C3 were `BLOCKED` on `gateway_busy_input`.

## Change

**1. H-C8 Gateway entry** (`server_engine/hive_busy_gateway.py`, built by the #1494 lane and carried here as `f3d223c9`).
- **Routing.** `digitalmate.request` sends the five actions to the entry before `EngineRequest` validation. Without a Hive Bee runtime they are refused as before.
- **Wire shape.** Requests and receipts match the #1297 fixtures. Params are checked exactly. `room_id` must be the Home. A receipt is `{operation_id, intent, status, run_id, queue_seq, successor_run_id, resume, draft_kept, replayed}`. `operation.get` returns the same receipt without `replayed`.
- **One acceptance per operation ID.** The Store's `HiveBusyControls` decides acceptance, and the entry serialises requests per ID. A resend goes to the Store only: it replays the receipt, or reads `CONFLICT` for edited parameters. It is never delivered to the running step again.
- **Declared controls only.** `snapshot["busy_controls"]` lists `steer` (with the Bee effect gate), `answer` (with the Host answer edge) and `stop`. `queue` and `preempt` are false until #1597. An undeclared control is refused with `BUSY_CONTROL_UNSUPPORTED`, and nothing is recorded.

**2. The user's steer is Beebou's SteerTask** (`UserSteerAdmission`, new in this PR).
- HIVE1 lets a Bee receive input only from Beebou. Before the effect gate steers, the entry admits the steer as Beebou's `SteerTask` of that task through the same Bot Repository directory and `AdmissionReceiver` that Beebou's own dispatch uses.
- The text is the user's, verbatim. The message ID is the operation ID. `execution_ref` is `hive-user-steer:<operation_id>`, so it is marked as the user's.
- It applies only when the Run is running at the given generation, and only for tasks this Beebou dispatched (otherwise `BAD_PARAMS` `task_ref`/`not_dispatched_by_beebou`). A full steer quota is `BUSY`, and an unknown admission is `RECEIPT_UNKNOWN` (retryable).
- No model is called. The Store consumes the admitted input when the steer is `APPLIED` (`_consume_applied_steers`).

**3. Beebou's context records it** (`HiveStore.claim_beebou_context`, §7a).
- Beebou's next turn gets one user-origin data message per accepted user steer (control `PENDING_APPLY` or `APPLIED`). The message is a label line plus `{kind, bee_id, task_ref, operation_id, text, sent_at_ms}`. It is told once, the same way as eviction notices.
- A stale, closed or conflicting steer is never told.
- New tunables in `hive_store.toml` `[beebou_context]`: `user_steer_label` and `user_steer_notes_per_turn = 8`.

**4. Runner rows: not in this PR.** The SC02 rows belong to hive3-qa (#1497 and #1535). The row patch I measured with goes to the coordinator for #1535. It does the following:
- publishes `gateway_busy_input` (`HiveBusyGateway.request/controls`, `UserSteerAdmission.admit`);
- publishes `manager_busy_input` (`BeeEffectGate.steer/release_lane`, the one-acceptance owner; the coordinator should confirm this mapping);
- makes SC02-C2 rerun the 11 `test_phase3_busy_gateway` owner tests plus the two Stop tests;
- reports SC02-C3 `NOT_RUN` "deferred to v3.5" through an `Assertion.deferred` field.

## Tests

`tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_busy_gateway.py` has 12 tests. These are real: the Hive Store and repository, BotTools Delivery, the Bot Repository directory and `AdmissionReceiver`, effects-mode Bee execution with `BeeEffectGate` and `WorkSwarmAdapter`, the Host answer edge, Beebou context claim and commit, and the Bridge install path. These are controlled: the WorkSwarm wire (held turn, `chat.input_received`, `chat.output_phase`), the isolation witness and the Bee question.

- **Lost ACK.** The resend replays `PENDING_APPLY` (`replayed: true`). The runtime got one steer, and the Store holds one control and one SteerTask input.
- **Same ID, other text.** An edited resend reads `CONFLICT` and delivers nothing.
- **Stale run.** A steer after Stop reads `TARGET_STALE` with the draft kept, and its replay matches. A steer for another run generation admits no SteerTask and is never told to Beebou.
- **SteerTask.** The input row is `bot:<beebou>` with `hive-user-steer:<op>` and the user's text verbatim. Beebou's next turn shows the note before its source message. After commit, the following turn does not repeat it.
- **APPLIED.** Once the step consumes the steer, `operation.get` reads `APPLIED` with the Host witness `…:<session>:<steer>:<phase>`.
- Also covered: double press, a task from another Beebou, malformed or undeclared requests, the question-card answer, and the Bridge declaration.

## Results at `c7b4857b` (HK, hk-longjianyu; this PR's code plus the #1535 row patch, which `b0b29a06` then removed)

- **G5 installed wheel**: `python3.13 tests/scenarios/run_hive.py --gate G5 --source wheel --scenario-python $PWD/.hive-deps-venv/bin/python --base-ref origin/main`
  - `PASS SC02-C2` with `cli_startup`, `store_busy`, `bee_stop`, `gateway_busy_input` and `manager_busy_input` all real, 3 labelled stand-ins, evidence 13.
  - `NOT_RUN SC02-C3 deferred to v3.5`.
  - Summary `{'PASS': 7, 'FAIL': 0, 'BLOCKED': 6, 'NOT_RUN': 1}`. The six BLOCKED rows are the SC04/SC05 rows owned by other lanes.
- **G5 checkout** (`--prepare-deps`, at `bd294826`): the same rows apart from two of the new tests, which a test helper broke; `c7b4857b` fixes it.
- **Suites:**
  - `test_phase3_busy_gateway`: 12 OK.
  - Phase 2 Beebou, Bee, Stop, steer and text-flow scenario modules: 89 OK, 1 skipped.
  - `test_session_proximity_hive_busy` and the Store suites: 21 OK.
  - `tests/scenarios/test_hive_runner` (with the row patch): 30 OK.
- **Architecture check**: 0 findings.
- **Known failure on hive3, not from this PR**: `test_hive_1243_bee_session_wire::test_every_new_code_is_pending_and_every_pending_code_is_used` fails on `SHARED_HOME_RESET_REFUSED` (#1576 adopted it into `ErrorCode` but it is still listed as pending). This PR adds no `ErrorCode`.

No new wire names. The internal names `hive-user-steer:`, `user_steer` and `not_dispatched_by_beebou` are not part of the H-C8 wire.

Integration PR for Project Hive Phase 3 (tracker #1533). It takes `hive/hive3-integration` to main in one merge commit, the same way HIVE1 used #1336 and HIVE2 used #1421. Once it merges, the constituent PRs show as merged.

**What lands**
- Phase 3 product surfaces: client, artifacts, eval, history and memory backfill.
- The Router-free Hive build (#1596, from the verified test-3 build `916ad25`). It removes the old Router under #1313, and Beebou handles every ordinary Home turn.

**Gates**
- G5: the official checklist on the candidate head, using the installed wheel with the pinned WorkSwarm runtime (`WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`). Multi-device rows are `NOT_RUN`, deferred to v3.5 (Phase 3 delivery §7a).
- G6: SC06 cutover rows on the same head, plus the installed-release Router scan.
- Native: single-device journeys on the test-3 direct-instance QA build.

Draft until G5 and G6 pass. It's open now so main's CI runs on the integration head.

Note: GitHub Actions artifact storage is full, so upload steps fail repo-wide (#1578). Those reds are upload-only; the evidence is the HK installed-wheel receipts on #1533.

## Stacking

Stacked on #1561 `dc438e671`; review only the commits after it; lands through hive/hive3-integration.
The branch also merges #1561's later review commits (`59c30c6dc` F4, `6fae24dbb` F5) by merge commit, no rebase.
The commits to review are `4de649865`, `5655eb22b`, `52bb9810f` and `d57fcec8f`; the two merge commits only bring in #1561.

Issue: #1242 (G5 row SC04-A5, "revoke/delete block download and agent read and erase DM bytes; stale blocks but does not erase; restart resumes").

## What changed

- **`StoredErasureIntents`** (new adapter module `server_engine/engine_artifact_erasure.py`, next to the notices one). It implements the `ErasureIntents` port (`record`, `pending`, `complete`) on the engine Store table `artifact_erasure_intents`: `intent_id` PK, `producer_task_id`, `artifact_id`, `digest`, `reason`, `recorded_at`, `completed_at` NULL.
  - `record` is `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so it is idempotent by intent_id.
  - `completed_at` is set only after `holds()` proved the bytes gone. Rows are kept as local evidence.
- **Tombstone in the withdraw transaction.** `EngineService.invalidate` now writes each revoked or deleted task row (live and archived) inside a transaction that also runs a new `EngineService.withdraw_listeners` hook. `ArtifactErasureWorker` registers a listener there that records the task's intents, so the intent commits or rolls back with the withdrawal. `engine_service.py` imports nothing from `dm_bee_artifacts`.
- **`ArtifactErasureWorker`** (same module). It is created with the engine in `Bridge.__init__`, so its tombstone listener is in place before any request. Its loop starts at Gateway startup, wakes on each task write (Store listener), runs every `[erasure] interval_ms`, and closes with the other producers.
  - Each pass runs the reconciliation repair pass, then `ErasureWorker(StoredErasureIntents, BeeArtifactSource, settings)`.
  - After a pass with an ERASED outcome it runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.
  - It sets `PRAGMA secure_delete` on the engine Store connection from `[erasure] secure_delete`.
- **Hard delete.** An intent whose task has no live or archived row is resolved by its own content id. `BeeArtifactSource.erase` calls the new byte-owner operation `WorkSwarmArtifacts.erase_unreferenced(content_id)`. It uses the same live-holder, pending-lease and path-safety checks as `erase_withdrawn`. ERASED is reported only once `holds()` is false.
- **Serve-time checks** (every path that serves task-file bytes refuses `stale`, `revoked` and `deleted` at call time, including for a reference taken before the withdrawal):
  - `delivery.create` `_attachment`, by path or by digest;
  - `delivery.approve`, and `_send` both before the gate and again inside the `sending` transaction;
  - `file.render` (`Bridge._task_file`, the preview of a coding run's file), covering live and archived cards;
  - already checked at serve time: `artifact.read` (and `report_http` / `report_runtime`, which call it), the agent read `ArtifactReader`, and `_transfer_from_session` (active cards only).
- **Fail-safe for a failed tombstone (`d57fcec8f`).** `invalidate` commits the source row before the task transaction.
  - Every serving path above also refuses when `EngineService.withdrawn_by_source(task)` reports that a source the task read, itself or through a recalled conversation, is revoked or deleted: `engine_attachments.py` `read_artifact` and `BeeArtifactSource.committed`, `delivery.py` `create` / `_check_files`, and `server.py` `_task_file`.
  - The worker's first full pass calls `EngineService.repair_withdrawals()`. It invalidates again any revoked or deleted source whose reached task still holds a file that is not withdrawn.
- **Archived cards on revoke/delete.** `engine_service.py` lines 1697-1707 (see §7a below).
- **Registration.** `temp/bee-artifacts/ownership.json` gets a new adapter row `bee-artifacts-engine-erasure`, the Gateway (`legacy-mobile-gateway`) as its declared caller, and new public config symbols `ErasureSettings` and `load_erasure_settings`. No shared gate file is edited (`module-ownership.json`, `.github/ci-gates.json` and `tests/scenarios/run_hive.py` are untouched).
- **Tunables.** `artifacts.toml` `[erasure]` gains `page_size = 50`, `interval_ms = 5000` and `secure_delete = true`; `batch_size` stays.
  - `load_erasure_settings` requires all four keys and validates them (positive integers; `secure_delete` must be a TOML boolean).
  - `load_settings` accepts the worker keys but does not require them.
- **`FixtureErasureLedger` deleted.** The handoff SC04-A5 tests now use `StoredErasureIntents`.

## §7a decisions recorded (v3.1 withdrawal promise)

- **Withdrawal promise.** Withdrawal blocks every new model-bound read at call time, and each byte owner's worker erases its own bytes. Text a conversation already received is not removed afterwards.
- **Approved: archived-card change, `engine_service.py` lines 1697-1707 at `e14b92459` (1711-1720 at `52bb9810f`).** Revoke/delete used to purge only the text of an archived task, so its file card stayed `active` and `artifact.read` still served the bytes after the source was deleted (reproduced before the fix). The archived purge loop now sets the card state, as `withdraw()` does for live tasks, and writes the row with its tombstone in one transaction. This closes a read-after-revoke hole.
- **Approved: Store question 7.** The tombstone (erasure intent) is written in the withdraw transaction, and the post-commit reconciliation pass stays as the repair path. `secure_delete` is on by config, and a WAL checkpoint follows each erasing pass.
- **Approved: Store question 11.** Every byte-serving path rechecks the card at serve time.
- **Erasure means absence from managed storage; backup retention follows Ops policy (v3.5 follow-up #1607).**

## Design choices

1. **Tombstone through a hook, not an import.** `EngineService` (a legacy inventoried module) gets `withdraw_listeners`, called inside the transaction that writes the withdrawn task row. A failing listener rolls that row back. The artifact adapter owns the intent SQL, so `engine_service.py` gains no dependency on the transition package and no domain write. Stale withdrawals call no listener.
2. **Reconciliation stays as repair.** Candidates are live or archived task rows that hold a revoked or deleted card and whose `artifacts` JSON differs from the one recorded in a separate `artifact_erasure_scans` table. This is the notices technique with its own table: sharing the notices table would couple erasure progress to broadcast progress.
   - The intents and the scan mark commit in one transaction.
   - The pass repairs any withdrawal written without the listener (a process without it, or an older release) and records the upgrade baseline.
   - It does not go through the principal's room check, because an erasure obligation does not depend on who is signed in.
3. **Archive cadence.** A Store-wake pass reads live rows plus recently archived ones (#1561 F4). Startup and interval passes read the whole archive, because `update_archived` keeps `archived_at`. Scan-row cleanup runs only on full passes (#1561 F5).
4. **Upgrade baseline.** The scans table starts empty, so the first pass records intents for versions withdrawn before the tables existed. Their bytes should still be erased.
5. **Erased only when verifiable.** ERASED requires that `erase` returns and `holds()` is false. Held (`LookupError`), failed or path-escaping (`OSError`, including `PermissionError`), unverifiable and unsupported-origin (`NotImplementedError`, for example an `artifact.publish` receipt) intents stay pending under their original id.
6. **Hard delete by content id.** The content id is `sha256(task, name, digest)`, so it names exactly this version's folder. No task row is needed to find it, and the digest is already bound into the id.
7. **`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, not PASSIVE.** PASSIVE copies frames back but leaves the old frames in the WAL file until they are overwritten, so page images from before the purge can stay on disk. TRUNCATE resets the WAL file to zero bytes. A busy result (a reader on an older snapshot) is logged, and the next erasing pass retries. The checkpoint runs once per pass that had an ERASED outcome, after those completions committed.
8. **`secure_delete` on the engine Store connection** that holds the artifact tables. The worker sets it at construction from config, explicitly ON or OFF.
9. **SQL is literal at every `execute` call**, including the PRAGMAs. There are no module-level SQL constants.

## Real vs FIXTURE

| Real | FIXTURE / SUBSTITUTE / not in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| EngineService and its SQLite Store (temporary folder, WAL mode), `EngineService.invalidate` / `withdraw` with `withdraw_listeners` (revoke, delete, stale; live and archived tasks), the result publication transaction, `WorkSwarmArtifacts` bytes, `erase_withdrawn`, `erase_unreferenced`, `holds` and sweep, `BeeArtifactSource`, `artifact.read`, `ArtifactReader`, the `snapshot` request, `DeliveryFlow` create/approve/`_send` with the harness gate, `StoredErasureIntents`, `ArtifactErasureWorker` with its Store wake, `secure_delete` and checkpoint, EngineService restart on the same folder, the production Gateway app (`configured_bridge` + `create_app`) with an authenticated WebSocket, `Bridge.file_render` | the `execute` callback standing in for a Bee runtime/model; the `artifact.publish` receipt entry (no ledger receipt); the Host `artifact_read` caller (`ArtifactReader` is called directly); the Slack transport (`FakeTransport`, as in `test_engine_delivery.py`); the renderer in the `file.render` check is a stub; the Gateway test writes the committed card as the result transaction does; the hard-delete test removes rows with SQL so that no sweep runs first. **Not in this PR:** backup expiry and replay (#1607), a verifiable deletion log for Ops. **Client rendering: not in this PR.** |

## G5 row spec (SC04-A5)

**Two erasure workers, one per byte owner (coordinator decision; not merged):**

| Byte owner | Worker | Status | Proving tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WorkSwarmArtifacts` bytes (engine tasks) | `ArtifactErasureWorker` + `StoredErasureIntents` (`server_engine/engine_artifact_erasure.py`, this PR) | proved here | the table below |
| `HiveDocumentBytes` (private Hive documents) | `HiveDocumentErasure` (`dm_bee_artifacts.artifacts.document_erasure`, wired in `server.py` on #1596) | **pending #1596 in hive3** | `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_document_store.py::DocumentStoreTests::test_erasure_recovers_original_withdrawal_after_lost_completion`, `::test_corrupt_receipt_never_completes_pending_erasures` (the HiveDocumentErasure cases; related: `::test_withdrawal_survives_restart_and_cannot_be_reactivated`, `::test_failed_withdrawal_transaction_leaves_no_fence_or_cleanup_obligation`) |

Note on the Hive half: on `hive/router-free-916ad25` (#1596 head `277c008aa`), `HiveDocumentErasure` and those tests come from `efaa999fb` ("reconcile withdrawn document bytes by original receipt"). `87f1c621` is the earlier `HiveDocumentBytes` prototype (`hive_document_bytes.py`, `test_hive_document_bytes.py`).

The rest of this section covers the WorkSwarm half. Tests live in `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/test_bee_artifact_erasure_store.py` (class `ErasureStoreTest` unless noted). Handoff tests are in `test_bee_artifact_handoff.py::BeeArtifactHandoffTest`.

| Intent durable at withdraw: written in the withdraw transaction; present when the process dies right after the commit and before any post-commit work; one per revoke/delete, replays add none; survives restart; repair pass for a withdrawal written without the tombstone; pre-existing withdrawn versions get intents | `test_the_intent_is_durable_when_the_process_dies_right_after_the_withdraw_commit`, `test_revoke_and_delete_each_record_exactly_one_durable_intent`, `test_a_withdrawal_written_without_the_tombstone_is_repaired_by_the_next_pass`, `test_versions_withdrawn_before_the_tables_existed_get_intents_on_upgrade`; handoff `test_revoked_and_deleted_block_download_and_agent_read_and_record_one_erasure_intent` |

- **Agent read:** `ArtifactReadError` with `revoked` / `deleted` for the named withdrawn version, and `version_unavailable` for an old artifact_id or digest.
- **Delivery:** `EngineError(FORBIDDEN)` at approve/send and `PermissionError` at create, both with `A file in this delivery was withdrawn …`.
- **`file.render`:** `PermissionError` `This file was withdrawn …`.
- **Snapshot:** the task card keeps the entry with `state` `revoked` / `deleted`.

Producer participants:

## Known limits

- On `stale`, an archived task's card is still not marked. This is unchanged and is for the Store owner.
- `invalidate` writes the source row before the task rows, each in its own transaction (pre-existing). If a tombstone write fails, the task row rolls back with it, but the source state change before it does not. **Fail-safe (`d57fcec8f`):** every serving path also refuses when a source the task read (itself or through a recalled conversation) is revoked or deleted (`EngineService.withdrawn_by_source`). The erasure worker's first full pass after a restart calls `EngineService.repair_withdrawals`, which invalidates such a source again, writing its cards, purge and tombstones, and the bytes are then erased. The serve-time source check does not follow memories: a task reached only through a memory the catalog invalidated is covered by the startup repair, not at serve time.
- The WAL checkpoint is skipped (logged) if a transaction is open on the connection when the pass runs, or if a reader keeps it busy. The next erasing pass retries.

## §7a: failed tombstone transaction (`9a073dd32`)
- **The line:** "A failed withdrawal tombstone transaction rolls back and re-raises to the caller on every path (user requests and engine-internal withdrawals). It is logged at error level with the source id and kind only (`engine_service.py` `_commit_withdrawal`). The source's own revoked/deleted state already refuses serve-time reads, and the next startup repair completes the withdrawal. Known limit: a task that reached the source only through a memory the catalog invalidated is not refused at serve time during that window; the startup repair covers it."
- **What the commit changes:** both task-row writes (live and archived) go through `_commit_withdrawal`.
- **New test:** `test_a_failed_tombstone_on_an_engine_internal_withdrawal_is_logged_and_raised`, for derived-source revocation. It fails on `d57fcec8f`.

1608.body:
**Hive Phase 3 constituent. Do not merge to `main` directly.** It lands through `hive/hive3-integration`.

Lane: #1312 (Step 3.4), SC05-M2. Base: `main` @ `14d284a6`. The branch also merges #1487 (`0531d9e6`, old-library tests) and #1488 (`ff7308bc`, the Phase 3 delivery doc), because this work updates both. Their changes show in this diff until they land, and the SC05-M2 commit is `1eef555f` onward.

## Why

Backfill fixes a clock-derived high water per scope and defers every later turn (`after_cutoff`, `in_flight`) to "the live path". No live path existed, and the three history sources shared no cutoff. After a restart, ingestion could take a turn twice or miss turns at the handoff. The G5 sign-off review (#1533) keeps SC05-M2 (shared authorized cutoff and durable ingestion cursor) as a G5 condition (§7a, 2026-11-16).

## Contract (Phase 3 delivery design §7b, v1)

1. **Sources.** `engine-tasks-v1`, `legacy-memory-v1` and `hive-beebou-v1` are authorized in `config/live.toml [sources] authorized`. A source that is off that list, fails its own principal check, or is not in the owner's recorded cutoff is refused with `PermissionError`, and nothing is written.
2. **One cutoff per owner.** `HandoffLedger.authorize(scope, sources)` records each source's mark and one shared `cutoff_at_ms`, in one transaction and once. A repeat returns the original (`resumed=True`). Backfill covers positions at or below the mark, and live ingestion covers positions above it. `BackfillRunner(handoff=…)` takes its high water from the ledger and does not call `mark()` again.
3. **Watermark cursor.** `live_page(scope, after, limit) -> LivePage(turns, watermark, complete)`. An in-flight turn holds the watermark just before itself. `LiveIngestion.advance` ingests with the backfill unit keys and `historical=False`. It then records the outcomes in `hl_items` and moves `hl_cursors` to the watermark in one transaction, after every provider ACK is committed. On restart, it resumes from the cursor and skips recorded `(source_key, source_rev)`. `query_unit` runs before ingest, so a unit already held is never sent twice. A lost ACK is resolved with `query_unit`.
4. **Corrections.** The successor carries `supersedes`. The provider withdraws the published original, or marks a staged one superseded.

## Store API note for #1311 (please review, and reopen if needed)

- **New:** `HiveStore.read_beebou_history(scope, *, after_seq, limit, host) -> (entries, watermark)`, delegated by `SQLiteSessionRepository`.
- **Shape:**
  - Read-only and authenticated with `authenticated_host`.
  - It checks the scope's workspace.
  - It runs one plain literal SQL statement, so it reads one snapshot.
  - `limit` must be at most `[tasks] page_limit`.
  - **No schema change.**
- **Entries:** Beebou `user` inputs (`kind='user'` and a session with `role='beebou'`) of this principal, in seq order. Each `BeebouHistoryEntry` carries `seq, session_ref, bot_id, message_id, text, created_at_ms, consumed, consume_kind, consume_witness, run_id, state, reply`. `reply` is the COMPLETED answer or the settled failure notice.
- **Watermark:** the lowest unconsumed seq minus one, otherwise the highest seq, or 0 when there are no inputs.
- **Deviation:** it is synchronous, unlike the async `read_*` calls. The history ports it serves (`HistorySource.page`/`current`, `BackfillRunner.begin`/`progress`) are synchronous. Like the async reads, it never awaits anything.
- **Decided by the #1312 lane** because the Store owner was unavailable, and recorded in §7a. #1311 may reopen it.

## Deviations from the v1 design

1. **The legacy task mark is pulled back before in-flight tasks.** For a source bound to `engine-tasks-v1`, the clock mark is pulled back to just before the first eligible task that is still in flight at the cutoff.
   - Why: with a pure clock mark, backfill defers that task as `in_flight`, and live ingestion, which starts above the mark, would never see it. That is the gap this contract exists to close.
   - Test: `test_sc05_m2_legacy_task_in_flight_at_the_cutoff_is_live_ingestions_once_it_settles`.
2. **The Beebou mark's `cutoff_at_ms` is the read instant**, never earlier than the shared cutoff. Its boundary is the seq position. This only keeps backfill's time re-check from deferring Beebou turns at or below the mark.
3. **`read_beebou_history` is synchronous** (see the Store note).
4. **Per-source backfill progress files** when `handoff=` is given (`hive-history-backfill.<source_id>.sqlite3`).

Not taken: the coordinator's fallback, which would have disabled the legacy sources with an `enabled` flag. The full legacy cursor is green.

**F1 (high, silent loss), fixed.**
- **The gap.** `legacy-memory-v1` positions a record by `updated_at`, but the review decision (`MemoryStore.put` with a new `review_status`) left `updated_at` unchanged. A proposal pending at the cutoff and approved after backfill passed it was taken by neither path.
- **No decided-at.** The store has a `memory_reviews.decided_at` column, but nothing writes it.
- **The fix.** `put()` now bumps `updated_at` when `review_status` changes. This matches `apply()`, whose every revision already sets `updated_at = now_ts()`. No schema change, and no watermark is held on pending records.
- **Every reader of a server `MemoryEntry.updated_at`** (searched across `agent_bridge/src`, `temp/*/src`, `server`):
  - `memory_agent.py`: load (`row_to_entry`), the JSON import, `put()` persistence, and `apply()`/`_revise`, which already bump it on every revision.
  - `hive_memory_history.py` (`LegacyHistorySource`): the live and backfill position key, and `source_rev`. The bump moves an approved record above the mark (the fix itself) and gives it a new revision.
  - Nothing sorts by it, shows it in a UI, or syncs on it. The client's `updated_at` hits are the phone's own local memory store, not this server store.
- **Superseding.** A record moving from approved to superseded is also bumped, but it is no longer approved, so neither path pages it, and its successor's `supersedes` withdraws it as before.

**F3, fixed.** `HiveBeebouHistorySource` fails at construction with a config error naming both values when `live.toml [page] size` exceeds `hive_store.toml [tasks] page_limit`. No silent clamp.

**F2, fixed.** A repeated `HandoffLedger.authorize` that names a source the recorded cutoff lacks raises `HandoffSourcesChanged`, naming the missing and the recorded sources, instead of silently returning the smaller record. Joining a new source to an existing cutoff is not supported yet.

针对 #1571 的端侧高耗电反馈，先加入可与 DevEco Profiler 时间轴对齐的活动日志，帮助区分会话、网络、语音、定位、头像动画和发现页任务的活动。此草稿不声称已经测出模块功耗或确定耗电根因。

- 只输出固定事件名、时间和汇总计数；复用已有事件，不新增周期定时器。限流并聚合日志，不记录对话、音频、坐标、账号、任务标识、URL 或异常文本。
- 启用、停止、字段口径和采集步骤见 [端侧功耗分析打点](docs/guides/development/device-power-diagnostics.md)。这些活动标记不是电量、电流或 CPU 时间，必须与真机 Profiler 测量结合分析。

本次只修改端侧、测试和文档，不修改云侧代码、权限声明或现有功能逻辑。

## 验证

- `hvigorw --mode module -p product=default -p buildMode=debug assembleHap --no-daemon`：调试 HAP 构建通过（未签名）。
- 端侧日志、会话、连接、动画、语音、定位、权限、发现页及相关回归共 25 个 Node 测试文件：324 项通过，1 项浏览器布局测试因本机未安装 Playwright 而跳过。
- 尚未运行依赖设备的 Hypium 测试，也未在真机验证日志或采集 Profiler 曲线。需要用经授权的调试设备执行真实场景采集，检查开关、各模块打点及日志开销，并保存曲线和验收截图。

Follow-up to #1557 (stacked: #1557's head `0b40d0e4` plus the commits after it; review those). Refs #1496.

## Root cause
The #1557 pinned-runtime journey hung 120 s in phase 2. The product rejected a tool-call ID the Session had already used.
`temp/hive-beebou/src/dm_hive_beebou/harness/normal.py` seeded `seen_call_ids` from every earlier assistant message and raised `ValueError("model returned an invalid tool call")` for a repeat (old lines 84 and 114). The scripted second-turn dispatch used `call-0`, which turn 1's `list_bees` had used. Real gateways do the same: some restart at `call_0` in every response (see `stream_event_rail.py:379`). So the second Beebou turn that calls a tool failed (`dm_hive_beebou_turn_failures` attempt 1 retry, attempt 2 settled with the resend notice), nothing was dispatched, and the `unavailable` frame the test awaited never existed. `exchange()` had read the reply and then waited 120 s for the frame.

The unavailable path itself was checked on the real Store and is sound: `ready_for` -> `BindingConflict` -> `read_unavailable_candidates` -> `commit_unavailable_result` -> notice -> `unavailable` frame. Real dispatched rows match `read_unavailable_candidates`.

## Fix
- `normal.py`: `_unique_calls` validates the calls and renames an ID the context already holds to `<id>~<n>` (smallest unused). Call, tool result and the Host's per-call operation ID (`tool_operation_id(scope, beebou, message_id, call_id)`; plan rows keyed by ordinal and call id) stay one-to-one. Two calls with one ID inside one message stay invalid. `quick.py` `run_second_quick` kept one `seen` set across all responses of a run and failed the same way, so it uses the same renaming (shared `harness/call_ids.py`), with a test.
- The journey's scripted dispatch deliberately keeps the repeated `call-0`. `exchange()` now fails after the reply with the reply and frames seen (20 s grace; 120 s for phase 1, where the Bee runs a real turn).

## Tests
- `temp/hive-beebou/tests/test_beebou_harness.py::test_a_tool_call_id_reused_across_responses_and_turns_is_renamed_not_rejected`: repeats within a turn, across turns, and the in-message duplicate. Fails before the fix (ValueError), passes after.
- New `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_bee_unavailable_offline.py`: phase 2 of the journey on the real CLI assembly, `create_app` WebSocket, v3.1 Registry/Host, Hive Store and publisher. Only the owned WorkSwarm process is a labelled stand-in (reports ready, runs no turn). Both queued tasks end unavailable with one terminal and one notice each, and Beebou answers the next turn. Fails before the fix after 25 s ("no frame satisfied the wait after the reply", reply `status: failed`), passes in about 4 s after (3/3).
- Beebou package tests 17 pass, hive-runtime Beebou tests 12 pass, scenario `test_phase2_beebou_*` (model, dispatch target, failed turn, done context) 27 pass.
- Real runtime: the journey `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_bee_unavailable_runtime.py` passes on the pinned WorkSwarm source (`0d685750`, wheels of the `be000e5e85ed` server-env), `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`, ports 19100-19102: OK in 49 s on head `437766144`. Its first rerun failed only `bee_calls 3 != 2`: every runtime start sends an image-capability probe (non-stream, one user message with a tiny PNG, no tools) that the test counted as a Bee turn; `dm_hive_runs` stayed 1. The probe is now counted separately.
- Beebou quick-reply test `test_second_quick_renames_a_tool_call_id_a_gateway_repeats_in_the_next_response` fails before the `quick.py` change, passes after.

1612.body:
## Stacking

Stacked on #1561 `6fae24dbb` (which is stacked on #1296). Review only the commits after `6fae24dbb`: `16bcb9c31` (the tool) and `3837f1b21` (the coordinator's decisions on this PR). This lands through `hive/hive3-integration`. `main` lacks `dm_bee_artifacts`, which is why it is stacked.

Issue #1242, G5 row SC04-A3, engine tasks. The Host `artifact_read` caller is now real. It replaces the test-only `HostArtifactReadSubstitute`.

## What changed

- **Tool.** `native_artifact_read(producer_task_id, artifact_id, digest, offset, limit)` is a tool on the `digitalmate` MCP server (`engine_tools_mcp`). WorkSwarm installs this server for each engine task execution with a signed tool token (`workswarm_adapter._install_tool_server`).
  - It posts `artifact.agent_read`, which is a new entry in `TOOL_ACTIONS` and in the contract `ACTIONS`.
  - It is listed only when `[host_read] model_reads` is true. Under the shipped config `build_server` does not register it, and the `native_artifact_read` sentence is left out of the server instructions.
  - It is listed as ungated in `engine_runtimes/base.py`, because the bridge binds and checks it.
  - Reading the switch adds a `callers` entry: `legacy-plugin` (the owner of `engine_tools_mcp`) may use `bee-artifacts-config`. If `dm_bee_artifacts` cannot be imported, the tool stays unlisted (fail closed).
  - With an empty `artifact_id`/`digest`, it lists the producer's active versions, capped by `[model_read] max_refs_per_result`.
- **Adapter.** `server_engine/engine_artifact_read.py` is a new module, registered as `bee-artifacts-engine-read` in `temp/bee-artifacts/ownership.json`. Its one declared caller is the Gateway (`legacy-mobile-gateway`), which installs it in `Bridge.__init__`; that is three added lines in `server.py`.
  - It is translation only, over `ArtifactReader` and `BeeArtifactSource`.
  - Its relation port also requires both tasks to be visible to the principal.
- **Core.** `ArtifactReader.read` now re-checks the relation, the committed state and the digest after the bytes are opened and decoded. A withdrawal, rewrite or lost relation committed in that window refuses the read. `ArtifactReader.versions` is new.
- **Contract.** `EngineRequest` gains `producer_task`, `artifact_digest`, `byte_offset` and `byte_limit`. There is no reader field.
  - The producer field deliberately has no `_id` suffix. The engine's generic `check_room_writes` checks every `*_id` field before a handler runs, and would answer a cross-user producer with `FORBIDDEN: Room is unavailable…`. Without the suffix, the handler's relation port refuses it exactly as it refuses a missing producer. The model-facing tool argument is still called `producer_task_id`.
- **Tool tokens only.** `dispatch_tool` sets `TOOL_SCOPE`, a `ContextVar` in the adapter, to the token's task around its dispatch. `artifact.agent_read` refuses any request whose `task_id` is not that scope: an owner token, a guest, or an in-process `engine.request`. Owner clients keep their own read paths (`artifact.read`, the task card).
- **Config.** A new, additive `[host_read] model_reads = false` section in `artifacts.toml` (`load_host_read_settings`). See the withdrawal promise below.
- **Tests.**
  - `HostArtifactReadSubstitute` and `test_host_artifact_read_refusals` are removed from `test_bee_artifact_handoff.py`. Every case they held is now covered through the real path in `test_bee_artifact_host_read.py`.
  - `test_cross_task_…` and `test_path_escape_…` stay as direct `ArtifactReader` vectors.
  - `test_engine_tools_mcp.py`'s exact tool-name set gains `native_artifact_read`.
- **Docs.** The SC04-A3 row and a new "Host `artifact_read`" section in `temp/bee-artifacts/README.md`.

## How the reader identity is bound

1. The model calls `native_artifact_read`. The tool server's `BridgeSocket` sends the execution's tool token, `digitalmate-tool.<task>.<epoch>.<hmac>`.
2. The Gateway (`websocket` → `tool_task` → `dispatch_tool`) then:
   - accepts only loopback requests with no `Origin`;
   - admits only `TOOL_ACTIONS`;
   - refuses any `task_id`/`parent_task_id` other than the token's task;
   - refuses a token from an earlier `execution_epoch`;
   - `_bind_tool_scope` writes the token's task into `task_id`;
   - and it sets `TOOL_SCOPE` to that task for the duration of the dispatch.
3. The engine's `check_room_writes` checks every `*_id` against the principal's rooms.
4. The `artifact.agent_read` handler requires `task_id == TOOL_SCOPE` and uses that task as `ReaderIdentity`. A request without a tool token is refused: `artifact_read refused: not_authorized: artifact_read accepts only a task's tool token`.

The model supplies only the producer task, the artifact id, the digest and the page. `EngineRequest` is `extra="forbid"`, so a `reader_task_id` argument is refused. All of this is tested in `test_the_reader_is_the_bound_task_and_never_a_model_argument`.

## Withdrawal promise (v3.1 decision 7a)

- **Guaranteed:** a withdrawal (`EngineService.invalidate` with stale, revoked or deleted) refuses every new model-bound read at call time.
  - That includes a read that names a saved version or digest, and a read whose bytes were already open when the withdrawal committed (the prototype `5e71ea909` leak).
  - The byte owner's worker erases the stored bytes (SC04-A5, separate PR).
- **Not guaranteed:** text a conversation (agent, Bee or Beebou) has already received is not removed afterwards. It leaves only through a scoped reset, Session eviction or conversation deletion. No test here claims otherwise.
- **Ships off.** With `[host_read] model_reads = false` in the bundled `artifacts.toml`, the MCP server does not register or list `native_artifact_read`. As a second layer for a stale tool list, the Gateway refuses any call with `artifact_read refused: disabled:` before any lookup. This holds until a real fence exists.
- **In-process sessions.** In-process DigitalMate sessions have no artifact_read in v3.1 (deferred to v3.5); model reads are off by default anyway.
  - The tests turn reads on in their own FIXTURE `artifacts.toml`, loaded by the production loader.
  - `test_the_shipped_configuration_keeps_model_reads_off` pins the shipped default.
- **Nothing cached.** The path keeps no text, page or extraction: `ArtifactReader` is built per call and returns what it read just now, after the re-check.

## Real vs FIXTURE

| Participant | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Production Gateway app (`configured_bridge` + `create_app`) on a loopback `TestServer`; the `/digitalmate/ws` socket | REAL |
| `native_artifact_read` through `build_server(EngineTools(BridgeSocket(...)))` and `FastMCP.call_tool`; signed per-execution tool token | REAL (the model is the test calling the tool in process instead of over stdio) |
| `dispatch_tool`, `_bind_tool_scope`, `check_room_writes`, `artifact.agent_read` → `ArtifactReader` → `BeeArtifactSource` → engine Store + `WorkSwarmArtifacts` bytes | REAL |
| Parent → child relation: router `agent.ask` sent with the parent's tool token (writes the `Question` and `child.parent_task_id`) | REAL |
| `EngineService.invalidate` (stale/revoked/deleted), `artifact.read` download | REAL |
| Child's file delivery and result commit (bytes stored through the real byte owner, then the card is written as the result transaction writes it) | FIXTURE: the scripted backend produces no files and its child asks a clarifying question, so the ask times out |
| Parent runs as agent `github` | FIXTURE: `digitalmate` cannot ask itself in the scripted catalog |
| Cross-user room and its relation records | FIXTURE: one principal per engine workspace |
| `artifacts.toml` with `model_reads = true` and small `[model_read]` limits; tampered bytes, symlinks and record paths | FIXTURE |

## G5 row spec: SC04-A3 (engine tasks)

**Row:** Beebou or an agent reads through Host control. An unrelated task, a cross-user reader, a revoked version, a wrong version or hash, a path escape and an over-limit read are each refused. Real participant: the Host `artifact_read` caller.

**Promise (decision 7a):**
- A withdrawal refuses every new model-bound read at call time, and SC04-A5's worker erases the bytes.
- Text a conversation already received is not recalled; it leaves through scoped reset, Session eviction or conversation deletion.
- Reads ship off (`[host_read] model_reads = false`). This row proves the read and refusal mechanics with reads enabled in the test config.

All tests are in `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/test_bee_artifact_host_read.py` (`HostArtifactReadGatewayTest`) unless marked "core", which means `temp/bee-artifacts/tests/test_bee_artifacts_host_read.py`.

| Assertion | Proving test | Refusal seen by the model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allowed read: the asking task reads paged UTF-8 text as itself; pages end on character boundaries; the page is capped by `[model_read] max_text_bytes` | `test_the_asking_task_reads_paged_text_as_itself_through_its_tool_token` | `bad_range` (offset mid-character, negative) |
| The reader is the Host-bound task, never a model argument; an earlier execution's token is refused | `test_the_reader_is_the_bound_task_and_never_a_model_argument` | `FORBIDDEN: A tool token acts only for the task it was issued to`, `BAD_PARAMS` (extra reader field), `not_authorized`, `earlier execution` |
| Tool tokens only: an owner-token call on the same Gateway socket and an in-process call are refused; the owner's `artifact.read` download still works; a tool-token call still reads | `test_only_a_tool_token_reads_and_owner_clients_keep_their_own_read_paths` | `not_authorized: artifact_read accepts only a task's tool token` |
| Unrelated task (a stranger, the child reading its parent, a nonexistent producer) | `test_unrelated_and_cross_user_readers_are_refused_before_any_lookup` | `not_authorized` |
| Cross-user producer, indistinguishable from a missing one | same test | `not_authorized`; the read and the listing errors are byte-identical to a missing producer's (`Error executing tool native_artifact_read: FORBIDDEN: artifact_read refused: not_authorized: This task was not dispatched by the reader`), with no `Room is unavailable`; another user's tool token: `no longer exists` |
| Revoked, deleted and stale | `test_stale_revoked_and_deleted_versions_are_refused` | `revoked` / `deleted` / `stale`; the listing is empty |
| Wrong version or digest | `test_wrong_version_digest_path_escape_and_over_limit_are_refused` | `version_unavailable` |
| Path escape | same test | `bad_reference` (traversal id or digest), `path_escape` (symlinked blob, record path outside the folder) |
| Hash mismatch | same test | `hash_mismatch` |
| Over limit (`max_object_bytes`) | same test | `too_large` |
| Binary, UTF-16 and non-WorkSwarm (`artifact.publish` receipt) versions | `test_binary_and_non_workswarm_versions_return_metadata_only` | none: metadata only, no `text` |
| Withdrawal refuses every later read at call time, after the text was read and any cache populated; a saved copy of the old digest and a fresh tool server are refused too; the download is refused (revoked, deleted) | `test_withdrawal_refuses_every_later_read_at_call_time` | `revoked` / `deleted`, and no bytes or text in the error |
| A withdrawal committed while the bytes are open refuses that read (the `5e71ea909` leak) | `test_a_withdrawal_committed_while_the_bytes_are_open_refuses_that_read`; core `test_a_change_committed_while_the_bytes_are_open_refuses_the_read` | `revoked` (also deleted, stale, rewrite and lost relation in core) |
| A saved reference to a replaced version is refused | `test_a_saved_reference_to_a_replaced_version_is_refused` | `version_unavailable` |
| Shipped default: model reads off. The tool is not listed under the bundled config and is listed when the flag is true; a stale tool list called while the flag is false is refused by the Gateway | `test_the_shipped_configuration_keeps_model_reads_off`; core `test_model_reads_ship_off_and_accept_only_true_or_false` | `Unknown tool` (not listed), then `disabled` (Gateway) |
| Listing is relation-checked, active only, bounded | core `test_versions_lists_only_active_committed_entries_after_the_relation_check` | `not_authorized`, `not_found` |

**Producer participants (module and role):**
- `server_engine/engine_router.py` `Router.ask`: real; records the `agent.ask` relation.
- `server_engine/workswarm_artifacts.py` `WorkSwarmArtifacts`: real byte owner (store, read, path containment, sweep).
- `server_engine/engine_service.py` `EngineService`: real Store records, `invalidate`/`withdraw`, room check.
- `server_engine/engine_attachments.py` `BeeArtifactSource`: real committed entries, bytes and relation.
- The child's result commit: FIXTURE.

Each test fails before this change: the tool, action and adapter did not exist. With the core's post-open re-check disabled, `test_a_withdrawal_committed_while_the_bytes_are_open_refuses_that_read` and the core re-check vector fail.

Each `3837f1b21` change was also reverted on its own, checked locally:
- tool-scope check reverted: `test_only_a_tool_token_reads_and_owner_clients_keep_their_own_read_paths` fails;
- field back to `producer_task_id`: `test_unrelated_and_cross_user_readers_are_refused_before_any_lookup` fails (plus the two tests that send raw frames);
- always-list: `test_the_shipped_configuration_keeps_model_reads_off` fails.

## Bee-produced artifacts: pending #1529

A Hive Bee producer is an independent root task. Its read relation comes from the #1223 dispatch record, not `agent.ask`, and the Hive Bee path on `main` is text-only. That case is not built here.

## Not covered and owner questions

- **In-process DigitalMate (jiuwen) session tools:** decided. They have no `artifact_read` in v3.1 (deferred to v3.5); see the withdrawal promise above.
- **Cross-user refusal code and owner-token callers:** decided and implemented in `3837f1b21` (byte-identical `not_authorized`; tool tokens only).
- **Turning reads on.** `[host_read] model_reads` stays `false` until a real fence exists (decision 7a). Who turns it on, and against which fence, is an owner decision.
- **Snapshot cost.** `artifact.agent_read` is not in `BARE_ANSWERS`, so the engine builds a snapshot that `dispatch_tool` then strips, as `artifact.read` does today. Adding it is a one-line `engine_service.py` change if wanted.
- **Shared files not edited** (as instructed): `module-ownership.json`, `.github/ci-gates.json`, `scripts/ci/*`, `tests/server/test_installed_package_proof.py`, `tests/scenarios/*`. CI enrollment of `temp/bee-artifacts/tests` (`enrolled.bee-artifacts`) is still the coordinator's row. `docs/implementations/migration/class-migration-checklist.json` lists `EngineTools` methods; it is not gate-enforced and was not updated.

## Local evidence

Head `3837f1b21`, base `6fae24dbb`, Python 3.12 venv (`uv pip install -e . -e 'harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge[agent]' pytest pytest-asyncio`), PYTHONPATH = Bridge `src` plus every `temp/*/src`. GitHub artifact uploads are quota-blocked, so the results are listed here.

| `python -m unittest discover -s temp/bee-artifacts/tests -p "test_bee_artifacts_*.py"` | 20 tests OK |
| `pytest tests/test_bee_artifact_host_read.py tests/test_bee_artifact_handoff.py` (Bridge) | 37 passed |
| `pytest tests/test_workswarm_artifacts.py tests/test_workswarm_adapter.py tests/test_workswarm_files.py tests/test_workswarm_flow.py tests/test_hive_result_gateway_startup.py tests/test_workspace_hosted_startup.py` | 137 passed |
| `pytest tests/test_engine_tools_mcp.py` | 5 failed / 33 passed, identical to base `6fae24dbb` and to `origin/main` `14d284a6a` in this local environment |
| `pytest tests/test_developer_setup.py tests/test_engine_memory_changes.py` (+ handoff, tools_mcp) | the same 20 failures on base and head (diffed); passed 215 → 214 only because the substitute test was removed |

"Unselected rooms still use a real legacy selector" is now "a non-Home room message is refused (`FORBIDDEN: Legacy task execution is disabled`) and the retired owner is not entered".

Four tests in `tests/server/test_contract_package.py` still expected the old inventory: 26/25 root files, 25 installed origins, 14 usage origins and an `engine_router` origin. Targets `hive/router-free-916ad25` (base 277c008a), not main.

## Leak

There are two model-bound Hive PDF text reads for Bees:

- `read_own_pdf`: `OwnHivePdfReader` (`temp/bee-artifacts/src/dm_bee_artifacts/artifacts/hive_pdf.py:28-53`).
- `read_home_input_pdf`: `BeeInputPdfReader` (`temp/hive-runtime/src/dm_hive_runtime/assembly/bee_input_pdf.py:8-50`).

At 277c008a they are wired in `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/src/server_engine/hive_bee_runtime.py:163-176`, with the `readers[...]` registration at `:234-240`.

Each read call is fenced when it is made. The gate checks the grant and binding before and after the read (`temp/hive-runtime/src/dm_hive_runtime/assembly/bee_effects.py:316-333`). The Store and byte owner refuse a withdrawn document (`session_proximity/hive_busy.py:2866` `withdraw_hive_document`), so a later call returns `Document unavailable.`

The gap is text that was already read. `bee_effects.py:333` returns it to the Bee model as a tool result, and nothing removes it after a withdrawal (`withdraw_hive_document`, or a revoked Home attachment hold):

1. **Bee Session conversation.** The tool result is part of the Bee turn's context. That context is committed to the Session Store (`temp/hive-runtime/src/dm_hive_runtime/assembly/bee_runtime.py:281-293` `commit_turn_context`) and sent to the model again on later steps and turns.
2. **Beebou context head.** When a Bee quotes or summarizes the text in a report or result, it enters Beebou's conversation. Beebou's retained context head is re-sent on each execution (`server_engine/session_proximity/context_execution.py:636-640`, `retained_context_head`).

Before this PR the gating was implicit:
- `read_own_pdf` turned on whenever a `create_hive_pdf` grant existed. That came from `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_DOCUMENT_PDF_*` or from a `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_DOCUMENT_FORMAT(S)` that includes `PDF` (`server.py:763-783` at 277c008a).
- `read_home_input_pdf` turned on with `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_INPUT_PDF_TRIAL=1` (`server.py:755-758`).

### v3.1 withdrawal promise (decision §7a)

Withdrawal blocks every new model-bound read at call time, and the owner's worker erases the bytes. Text that a Bee or Beebou conversation already received is not removed afterwards. It leaves only through scoped reset, Bee Session eviction or conversation deletion. That is why `model_reads` ships off by default until a real fence exists.

## Gate

- **Flag.** `temp/hive-runtime/src/dm_hive_runtime/config/bee_effects.toml` now has `[documents] model_reads = false`. It is read by `load_bee_effects` into `BeeEffectSettings.model_reads`, a required field with no default.
  - A missing key or table raises `KeyError`, the same as the loader's other keys.
  - A non-bool value raises `ValueError` in `__post_init__`.
  - It is not an env var and not a constant.
- **Assembly** (`hive_bee_runtime.py`).
  - `compose_bee_runtime` builds `OwnHivePdfReader` and the `read_own_pdf` tool only when `model_reads` is true.
  - It raises `ValueError` before any registration if it is given an `input_pdf_owner` while `model_reads` is false. Without that owner, `read_home_input_pdf` is never registered.
  - `create_hive_pdf` and the other `create_hive_*` grants are unchanged. Generation, listing and withdrawal still work.
  - New public `bee_effect_settings(effects=...)` is registered in `temp/hive-runtime/ownership.json`. The server reads the settings through it because `server.py` has no declared dependency on `hive-runtime-config`. The server passes the same object to `compose_bee_runtime`, so both see one value.
- **Server** (`server.py` `configure_hive_bee_runtime`).
  - Refuses startup with `ValueError` when `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_INPUT_PDF_TRIAL=1` and `model_reads` is false: "DIGITALMATE_HIVE_INPUT_PDF_TRIAL=1 requires Hive document model reads: set model_reads = true under [documents] in dm_hive_runtime bee_effects.toml".
  - With `model_reads` true, logs one WARNING: "Hive document model reads are enabled; a withdrawal does not fence text already read into a Bee or Beebou context."
- **Docs.**
  - `temp/bee-artifacts/docs/a3-hive-pdf-owner-boundary.md` has a new section on the gate and the known leak. It names both paths, the Bee Session conversation and Beebou's context head, and the §7a promise.
  - `temp/hive-runtime/README.md` links to that section.

## Tests

New tests. Each one fails at 277c008a and passes here. I checked this by restoring the four base source files over the new tests.

- `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_document_model_reads.py` goes through the real `configured_bridge` → `configure_hive_bee_runtime` → `compose_bee_runtime`, with the Bridge's real Store, Host, byte owner and effect gate. The WorkSwarm adapter is the unstarted owned one, so no process runs.
  - Default config with a `create_hive_pdf` grant: neither the advertised list nor the gate-admitted list has `read_own_pdf` or `read_home_input_pdf`, and no warning is logged. The test then commits a real PDF, reads its marker through the owner, and withdraws it with `withdraw_hive_document`. After that the owner read raises `LookupError`, and every read tool through the gate is refused as not allowlisted, with no marker.
  - Default config with `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_INPUT_PDF_TRIAL=1`: startup is refused.
  - `model_reads = true`: both tools are advertised and admitted, and the WARNING is logged exactly once. After withdrawal, read calls return `Document unavailable.` with no marker.
- `temp/hive-runtime/tests/test_bee_effects.py` `DocumentModelReadSettingsTests`:
  - the bundled default is `false`;
  - explicit `true` loads;
  - a missing key or table raises `KeyError`;
  - `"false"`, `"true"`, `0`, `1` and `[]` each raise `ValueError`.
- `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/hive_model_reads_support.py` (a helper, not a test module). `model_reads_enabled()` loads the bundled TOML with only `model_reads = true` set, and serves it to `server_engine.hive_bee_runtime`.

### Existing tests that now set the flag explicitly

- `tests/scenarios/hive/test_hive_owned_pdf_a3_read.py` (`read_own_pdf`)
- `tests/scenarios/hive/test_home_bee_input_pdf_trial.py` (`read_home_input_pdf`)

- `temp/hive-runtime/tests/test_bee_effects.py` `ScopedReaderGateTests`: sets `model_reads=True` on the settings it builds for the `read_own_pdf` reader

All five scenario tests are skipped here. They need the pinned WorkSwarm (`WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`).

Unchanged because they do not go through the gate:
- `test_hive_home_input_pdf.py` calls `configure_input_pdf` directly.
- `test_hive_document_store.py` uses `OwnHivePdfReader` directly.
- `test_home_bee_documents_trial.py` exercises only `create_hive_*`.

## Local evidence

All runs are at head `93ec8735`, local macOS, Python 3.12 venv (`uv pip install -e . -e 'harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge[agent]' pytest pytest-asyncio`). PYTHONPATH is agent_bridge `src`, every `temp/*/src`, agent_bridge `tests` and `tests/scenarios`. No WorkSwarm runtime, Mac Bee runtime, real model, HK or test-3 was used. GitHub artifact upload is quota-blocked, so the results are listed here.

| Command | Head 93ec8735 | Base 277c008a |
|---|---|---|
| `python3.13 tools/architecture/check.py --policy docs/implementations/migration/module-ownership.json --root .` | 0 findings (255 of 497 files checked) | n/a |
| `python -m pytest tests/architecture -q` | 231 passed, **5 failed** | the same 5 fail |
| `python -m pytest temp/hive-runtime/tests tests/scenarios/hive [+ new bridge test] --continue-on-collection-errors` | 341 passed, 99 skipped, 4 failed, 1 error | 334 passed, 99 skipped, 4 failed, 1 error |
| `python -m pytest harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests -k "test_hive_ or workswarm_bee_effects" --continue-on-collection-errors` | 247 passed, 78 failed, 44 errors | 244 passed, 78 failed, 44 errors |
| Touched tests: `test_hive_document_model_reads.py`, `test_bee_effects.py`, the touched scenario files except cross_owners, `test_hive_document_store.py`, `test_workswarm_bee_effects.py` | 37 passed, 27 skipped (pinned WorkSwarm) | n/a |
| New tests with the 4 base source files restored | n/a | all 8 fail (`read_own_pdf` offered; `DID NOT RAISE ValueError`; no `model_reads`) |

**No new failures.** The sorted FAILED/ERROR node lists of the two pytest suites are identical at base and head: 123 entries each, checked with `diff`. Head passes 10 more tests: 7 new ones in the first run, and the 3 new bridge tests again in the second.

The failures that remain exist on the Router-free base already and are outside this lane. Another session is fixing the stale tests.
- `tests/architecture`: `test_a01_enrollment::test_router_cannot_import_private_contract_helper` and `test_a02_enrollment::test_router_cannot_bypass_the_store_proxy_to_schema` (missing `server/router/contracts.py`); `test_domains::DomainWriterTests` x3.

- Bridge: mostly `ModuleNotFoundError: server_engine.engine_router` / `dm_sessions.routing` and "Hive Home requires results, turns, and a configured Beebou". `test_hive_home_input_pdf.py` cannot be collected at base (`dm_sessions.routing`).
- WorkSwarm-gated scenario tests (the 5 edited files among them) were skipped. They need `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1` and a pinned runtime, which were not used.

## Follow-up for a real fence

- Read results need a document identity, such as artifact id plus digest or the Home source id plus revision, recorded with the committed Bee context and anything derived into Beebou's context head.
- Withdrawal or a revoked hold must then redact or mask those spans in the Bee Session Store context and in Beebou's retained context head. The model must never see the text again, and replay or recovery must be handled. The alternative is to keep read text out of the committed conversation altogether.
- This needs an owner decision across Session Store (context), the Hive Bee runtime and Beebou. Until then, `model_reads` stays `false` outside controlled trials.
