Fixes #1616. Cut from hive3 `f322dd74` (PRs keep the main base; the diff to review is the one commit `c454e0091`). It merges cleanly onto `hive/hive3-integration` at `f322dd74` (`git merge-tree`: no conflicts).

## Problem
With every Bee slot held by a Bee with open work, `create_bee` and `activate_bee` return `CAPACITY_BUSY` as an ordinary tool result and the normal-turn loop keeps calling the model until the budget runs out (`BeebouHarness`, 12 calls). The turn settles failed with the generic resend notice, although resending cannot help.

## Fix (three layers)
1. **Host** (`server_engine/hive_beebou_tools.py`): `HiveBeebouTools` serves one turn. Its first `CAPACITY_BUSY` receipt is kept; every later `create_bee` / `activate_bee` of that turn returns a copy of it at once, before validation and with no Bot effect entry (no `generate_bee` / `activate_known_bee`, no admission, no Store claim). A new turn is a new instance, so it asks the Store again. Note: the receipt names the busy Bees only through its detail text and `list_bees` (it carries no Bee list today); the tool descriptions point the model at `list_bees`.
2. **Tool descriptions** (`dm_hive_beebou/selection.py`): `CAPACITY_BUSY` means tell the user which Bees are busy and that they can wait, or stop or answer one; do not retry in this turn.
3. **Settlement** (`session_proximity/hive_store.py`, `hive_store.toml`): a `harness` failure (budget exhausted) after a `CAPACITY_BUSY` plan result, with no other effect that ran, settles with the new `[beebou_turns] capacity_notice` (en and zh, in the existing TOML string register) instead of `failure_notice`. Another effect that ran keeps `effect_notice`; a non-harness failure keeps `failure_notice`. The `CAPACITY_BUSY` result is excluded from the "effected" test because it created nothing.

## Tests
- `tests/test_hive_beebou_capacity_loop.py` (new): replay on the real Store, Bot Repository, tool guard and grant, `HiveBeebouTools`, `BeebouHarness` and `HiveTurnStartup` with a model that never stops (slot capacity 0). Asserts exactly one `generate_bee` entry and no `activate_known_bee` entry, 12 identical `CAPACITY_BUSY` plan results, the settled reply is the capacity notice (not `failure_notice`, not `effect_notice`), kind `harness`; next turn makes its own admission attempt and commits; settlement matrix (capacity only, capacity plus another effect, non-harness kind, no capacity receipt).
- `tests/test_hive_create_bee_capacity.py`: per-turn latch on a real Store (capacity 1, one open task): the second `create_bee` and an `activate_bee` get a copy of the first receipt, no second Bot effect entry and no new activation claim; a new tools instance asks again.
- Fail before the fix: with the latch reverted the replay fails (`generate_bee` entered 6 times, `activate_known_bee` 6) and the unit test fails; with only the notice choice reverted the replay fails on the generic notice.
- Passing: Beebou package 20, agent_bridge `test_*hive*` / `*beebou*` / `*bee*` 362 passed (4 skipped, 7 xfailed), scenario `test_phase2_beebou_*` 34.
- No real-runtime run (slot is with behaviour QA).

> **Hive Phase 3 / H-R3 follow-up into the Router-free branch (`hive/router-free-916ad25`).** It goes into that branch, not `main`.

Two commits on `cfff8368` (after #1621):

## 1. `924f8d2e`: one failing history source never holds the others back (SC05-M2)

The coordinator asked whether the live cursors are per source. They are: each source has its own `hl_cursors` row, page and `commit_page` CAS, so a stuck (in-flight) cursor never blocks the others.

But `LiveIngestion.advance` read every source's page before ingesting any of them. So an exception from one source's read stopped every source for that pass. A persistently failing source (a Store error, a bad legacy record) would have starved the rest.

Now:
- **Refusals still stop the whole pass before anything is written** (`PermissionError`). That covers a source outside the owner's recorded cutoff, or one whose own scope check refuses the read.
- **Any other read or ingest failure stays with its source.** That source reports `retry_later` with its cursor unmoved, and the failure is logged with the source id. The other sources still advance in the same pass.

Test: `test_hive_memory_live.py::IsolationTests::test_sc05_m2_a_failing_source_never_holds_the_other_sources_back`. `engine-tasks-v1` fails on every read for three passes; `hive-beebou-v1` still ingests its post-cutoff turn and moves its cursor, and the failing source's cursor and items are unchanged. It fails without the change.

## 1b. `9e654c4d`: the coordinator's guards on the isolation

- **Refusals per source, at error level.** A `PermissionError` from one source no longer stops the whole pass. That covers a source that is not in the owner's recorded cutoff, and one whose own scope check refuses the read.
  - It becomes that source's `retry_later`, logged at **error** level with the source id and the error type only, never record content.
  - Nothing is written for that source (no cursor row, no items), and the other sources still advance.
  - The `live.toml` allow-list is still refused when `LiveIngestion` is built, before anything runs.
- **`LiveReport.consecutive_failures`** counts the passes in a row a source reported `retry_later`. It is per process and resets on success, so a stuck source shows up.
- **Only `Exception` is caught.** `asyncio.CancelledError` and `KeyboardInterrupt` propagate, so shutdown's cancel-and-await stays prompt (SC02-R1).
- **Tests:**
  - `CancellationTests::test_sc05_m2_cancelling_the_job_during_a_slow_source_returns_promptly`: `close()` returns in under 1 s during an hour-long provider call, and nothing is recorded. A `BaseException` catch fails it.
  - `RefusalTests` asserts per-source error-level refusals.
  - `IsolationTests` asserts the failure counts.
- **Results:** `test_hive_memory_live.py` 12 OK; hive-memory suite OK; startup and Store history tests 9 passed. The architecture check has only the base's 3 D8 findings.
- **Note:** a synchronous source read that blocks (`live_page` is a synchronous Store read bounded by `[page] size`) cannot be interrupted mid-call. Cancellation lands at the next await.

## 2. `469d0b93`: delete the retired reviewed-memory live relay (#1620)

Since #1621, Bridge startup runs `LiveIngestionJob`, and nothing starts or imports the earlier single-stream relay.

**Deleted:**
- `backfill/relay.py`, `backfill/reviewed_live.py` and `tests/test_hive_memory_relay.py`.
- The `SuccessorFeed` / `SuccessorPage` / `TruncatedHistoryLog` seam in `backfill/ports.py`.
- `ReviewedMemoryLiveSource` in `server_engine/hive_memory_history.py`.
- Their names in `temp/hive-memory/ownership.json`.
- The retired `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_REVIEWED_MEMORY_LIVE_TRIAL` setting in `test_hive_next_queue_with_grants.py` and `test_hive_next_home_cross_owners.py`.

**Kept:**
- `ReviewedMemoryHomeReader` (`hive.memory.reviewed.get`).
- `CurrentHistorySource` (the base of `HistorySource`).
- The startup log line for the retired switch.

**Docs:** the two relay proposals under `temp/hive-memory/docs` are marked superseded by §7b (one links to the other), and the README drops the relay rows.

**Nothing still refers to the deleted code.** A search for the module names, the seam names and `test_hive_memory_relay` over all `.py`, `.json`, `.toml` and `.yml` files finds nothing. That covers `ownership.json`, `module-ownership.json`, `.github/ci-gates.json` (the relay test was never a gate marker) and the scenario rows.

## Results

Run at `469d0b93` (python 3.13 with the Bridge dependencies; PYTHONPATH = repo root plus the ci-gates `sourcePaths`, `temp/beebou/src` and `tests/scenarios`; `NO_PROXY` set; short `TMPDIR`):

## Where the 4–10 s went
- The terminal write and the `done` input were two unrelated steps:
  - `HiveBusyControls.commit_text_result` sets `dm_hive_tasks.state='completed'` and writes the user result in one Store write.
  - Nothing then reported to Beebou. The Bee scheduler only publishes the user-facing frame (`publish`).
  - The Bee's `done` input to Beebou was created only by `HiveReportRecovery`, a periodic scan of completed tasks calling `report_committed`. Its pause is `[report_recovery] interval_ms = 10000` (`temp/hive-worker/.../bee_execution.toml`).
- So the lag is uniform on 0–10 s, which matches the issue: median 4.1 s, p90 8.3 s, max 9.6 s across 106 tasks.
- The report turn was not waiting on anything. Its input simply did not exist until the next scan.
- A second effect makes atomicity alone insufficient. `peek_beebou_inbox` and `drain_inbox` serve a pending user input before any pending Bee report. Even with the `done` committed at once, a user turn arriving in the window runs first.
- That turn reads `list_bees`. The roster's `tasks_at_hand` drops terminal tasks, so the Bee showed no task and no deliverable. This is exactly LANG-02's *"had no task or deliverable on record"*.

## Fix
1. **One fenced Store transaction.**
   - `HiveStore.enqueue_committed_report` runs inside `commit_text_result`'s write, right after the terminal UPDATE. It admits the `done` input and its accepted delivery receipt.
   - It uses the exact identity `report_committed` delivers through BotTools (new shared `committed_report_id`, same `_delivery()` fingerprint path). Report recovery therefore just replays the receipt: no duplicate input and no ID conflict.
   - It writes nothing, and recovery keeps the report, when the receiving checks cannot pass from Store rows: no ACTIVE Beebou binding, a foreign or retired Bee session, or an unknown realm.
   - It also writes nothing when the Bee already reported that same Run's `done` under its own ID.
   - A replayed commit made before this change gets its report on replay.
   - Beebou still consumes the input only after its fenced context commit, unchanged.
2. **Beebou's task view carries the result.**
   - `list_bees` now returns `results[]`: `{bee_id, task_ref, state, result}` for completed tasks whose `done` no committed Beebou context has consumed yet. It shows the newest first and is capped by the existing `task_page_limit`.
   - The `list_bees` tool description tells the model to answer a status question from it instead of dispatching again.
   - Once the `done` turn commits, the entry leaves the view.

No schema or migration change, no sleeps or polling, and no new tunables. The `interval_ms` comment now says the scan only retries.

## Tests
- `tests/test_hive_done_report_atomicity.py` (Store level, 7 tests):
  - the terminal and `done` input plus receipt are written together and claimable by Beebou;
  - a failure injected after the `done` insert rolls back the terminal, result and report;
  - recovery replays the receipt;
  - a replayed commit keeps one report;
  - a pre-fix commit gets its report on replay;
  - a Bee-sent `done` is not duplicated;
  - `unreported_results` holds the result until Beebou consumes it.
- `tests/test_hive_status_in_done_window.py`, the interleaved user turn:
  - Setup: real CLI `configured_bridge`, Beebou turn service, Store; labelled controlled model and Bee runtime. The Host commits the terminal, then the user asks "Is the book club plan done?" before the `done` turn.
  - **Before the fix** (src reverted, same test): `assert 'Not yet: the Bee has no output on record.' == 'Yes: Book club plan: …'`. This is the LANG-02 view.
  - **After:** the answer carries the result, no duplicate task is dispatched, the `done` turn still runs once, and the view then empties.
- Updated `test_hive_bee_induced_reply.py::test_done_from_an_old_run_never_triggers_beebou`, `test_hive_live_recovery_startup.py` and `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_bee_execution.py::test_committed_report_recovers_after_store_restart`. They asserted the old empty Inbox right after commit, which is the gap itself. They now expect the report at commit, and recovery replaying the same message ID.

## Local runs (macOS, python 3.13 venv)
- Bridge `test_hive*` + `test_session_proximity*` + `test_workswarm*`: 842 passed.
  - 7 failures that also fail on pristine main in this venv, all environmental (helper-process and engine-path probes).
  - Plus 1 failure that was mine and is now fixed.
- `temp/hive-*`, `temp/beebou`, `tests/scenarios/hive`: 549 passed.
  - `factory_observation` needs a short `TMPDIR` (AF_UNIX path limit).
- Merges cleanly onto hive3 `f322dd74`. On that merge, the #1615 tests and the touched suites pass. hive3's #1525 Bee-event shape is handled by the interleave test's controlled model.
- No real-runtime run (slot is with behaviour QA).

## Not in scope
- The Inbox's user-first ordering is unchanged.
- The LANG-02 report turn left `RUNNING` at case end is a separate observation.

1633.body:
Test-only. Targets `hive/router-free-916ad25`, based on `2fd7ad925` (merged in with a merge commit). It makes the #1242 SC04-A3 and SC04-A5 artifact tests run on the Router-free Bridge, without weakening any assertion.

## Failure

On `hive/router-free-916ad25` at `50ed29d01`, 12 artifact tests failed with `EngineError: FORBIDDEN "Legacy task execution is disabled"`:
- `harness/personal-agent/services/agent_bridge/tests/test_bee_artifact_host_read.py`: all 11 tests;
- `tests/test_bee_artifact_erasure_store.py::ArtifactErasureGatewayTest::test_a_revoked_workswarm_artifact_is_erased_by_the_started_gateway`.

## Cause

- The Router-free Bridge hard-codes `legacy_execution=False` (`server.py:498`, `server.py:579`).
- `EngineService.check_legacy_request` then refuses every action in `_LEGACY_EXECUTION_ACTIONS` (`engine_service.py:277`: `task.create`, `task.run`, `agent.ask`, …) with `require_legacy_execution` (`engine_service.py:2087`). The tests created their tasks with `task.create`, and the host-read tests asked with `agent.ask`.
- The host-read tests had a second, deeper blocker: the Router-free Gateway retires engine tool tokens.
  - `websocket()` (`server.py:4769-4770`) refuses a tool token with a 403, "Legacy room-task tool credentials are retired".
  - `dispatch_tool` (`server.py:993-994`) returns `FORBIDDEN "Legacy room-task tools are retired"` while legacy execution is off.
  - `artifact.agent_read` accepts tool tokens only (#1612), so in this build **no caller reaches it**. `artifact_read` has no engine-agent caller in the Router-free build: model reads are off by default (`[host_read] model_reads = false`), and a Bee caller is #1529 / v3.5.

## Port

**SC04-A5: `ArtifactErasureGatewayTest`** (`e425d3c3f`)
- Its three task rows are seeded, not created with `task.create`: the revoked report, the coding preview, and the tombstone-failure preview.
- They are written through `store.create` by the new FIXTURE helper `hive_home_profile.seed_legacy_task`.
- Bytes still go through the real WorkSwarm byte owner (`store_workswarm_file`, then the committed card), and the revoke through the real `EngineService.invalidate`.
- Every assertion is unchanged: erased by the started Gateway worker, bytes gone, the intent's `completed_at` set, the download refused, the revoked card in the Home snapshot, the preview refused at serve time, and the tombstone failure.

**SC04-A3: `HostArtifactReadGatewayTest`** (`44155f885`, coordinator option A)
- The 11 Gateway tool-path tests skip when the started bridge's `engine.legacy_execution_enabled` is false, the predicate `server.py` uses.
- Skip reason: "Router-free Gateway retires engine tool tokens (server.py:4769-4770 websocket, 993-994 dispatch_tool); port to the Bee-side caller is #1529".
- Every test body and assertion is unchanged; they still run wherever tool tokens exist.
- Once hive3 → main lands, main is Router-free too, so these 11 tests will skip on main as well. Porting them to the Bee-side caller is tracked in #1529.

**New: `tests/test_bee_artifact_host_read.py::RouterFreeArtifactReadUnreachableTest::test_no_tool_token_or_owner_call_reads_an_artifact_on_the_router_free_gateway`**

It runs on the Router-free Bridge and skips only where legacy execution, and so tool tokens, exist. It seeds a reader, a producer and the producer's committed file. As a positive control, the person's own `artifact.read` download returns the file, so a leak would show. Then it checks every layer:
- (a) A plain request to the tool socket gets 403 with "Legacy room-task tool credentials are retired"; `ws_connect` gets a 403 handshake; the real `BridgeSocket` tool transport cannot connect.
- (b) `dispatch_tool`, called with the token's scope, returns exactly `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "FORBIDDEN", "message": "Legacy room-task tools are retired"}}`.
- (c) An owner-token `artifact.agent_read` on the same socket is refused with `artifact_read refused: not_authorized: artifact_read accepts only a task's tool token`.
- In every case no file bytes or text come back: neither the text nor its head or tail, nor its base64 head, appears in any reply. The byte owner still holds the file, untouched.

## FIXTURE

| Stand-in | Stands in for | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hive_home_profile.seed_legacy_task` (Task row via `store.create`) | engine Task rows `task.create` would write; Router-free has them only in upgraded workspaces | `ArtifactErasureGatewayTest` (3 rows), `RouterFreeArtifactReadUnreachableTest` (reader, producer) |
| `Question` row via `store.create` (parent_task_id = reader, producing_run_id = producer) + `producer.parent_task_id` | the `agent.ask` relation the router writes | `RouterFreeArtifactReadUnreachableTest` |
| Result commit: bytes through the real `WorkSwarmArtifacts`, then the committed card via `store.update` | the result transaction of a WorkSwarm run (the scripted backend produces no files) | both |
| `FIXTURE-artifacts.toml` with `[host_read] model_reads = true` | an operator turning model reads on, so no refusal comes from the shipped default | `RouterFreeArtifactReadUnreachableTest` |

Refs #1575 · gate fix on main, not a Hive constituent. **Merge with a merge commit, not squash**: `ACTIVE_SOURCE_SHA` names this PR's first commit.

## Why

#1575's isolated `server-ut-st` proof is not a #1575 defect. The trusted gate ran **every enrolled suite in one attached capture**, bounded by a fixed 2 MiB live log (`LOG_LIMIT`) and a hard 1200 s ceiling in `server_active_output.capture`. With the `Path.home()` fixes, `bridge-context-configured-runtime` now runs the real WorkSwarm runtime in-process and logs legitimately. On native amd64 the whole run no longer fits in either bound:

| Measurement (native amd64 HK Pod, pinned `python:3.13.13-slim`, uid 1001, local Unix-socket Docker 27.5.1; candidate #1575 `dcea9448` on main `4cc3d9af`) | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Installed-contract phases at the start of every selector run (294/9/24/43 tests) | about 45 s |
| `architecture-shadow` (236 tests) | **684.6 s** |
| `bridge-context-configured` | 8 tests, 0.5 s |
| `bridge-context-configured-runtime` | about 7–10 s per runtime test; **2 MiB of log reached by about the 11th test**. Log sources: `jiuwenswarm.server.agent_ws_server` 925 lines, `…interface_deep` 829, `…e2a.wire_codec` 428, rich-formatted `openjiuwen.*` loggers about 64% of bytes |
| `--suite all` with the capture raised to 1200 s | `CaptureError` at the deadline while still inside `bridge-context-configured-runtime` |

The gate can't lower the candidate's log levels reliably. Three logging systems contribute (WorkSwarm reads `LOG_LEVEL` once at import; stdlib `openjiuwen.*` loggers go through a root rich handler; agent-core's YAML-configured loggers set their level on first use), and the tests clear `os.environ`. So the bounds move to configuration instead.

## What

- **One bounded capture per enrolled suite.** `server_active_entry.execute` reads the trusted registry (`.github/ci-gates.json`, bounded no-follow read) for the enrolled set and runs each enrolled suite in sorted order through the existing hardened flow (`execute_suite`). Each suite gets its own host task, output lease, `--suite NAME`, trusted collection and failure/journal reports under `reports/suites/<name>/`. The first failing suite stops the run, and the stderr line names it (`bounded active suite <name> failed: <Class>`). The name comes from the trusted registry, never from candidate output.
- **Per-suite bounds in config, reviewed ceilings in code.** The new trusted `.github/server-active-captures.json` gives each enrolled suite `{timeoutSeconds, logLimitBytes}`. It isn't in `ci-gates.json` because the contract package proof (`server_contract_package.registry_transition_rows`) pins that registry's keys and old rows exactly. `capture_plan` requires the file to cover exactly the enrolled suites, and refuses a missing, extra-keyed or non-integer bound, or any value above the reviewed ceilings in `server_active_output`: `CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MAX = 1800`, `LOG_LIMIT = 32 MiB` (the output tmpfs is 128 MiB). `capture()` checks against the ceilings, not a literal. `run_suite` passes the suite's `log_limit` as the live capture maximum and sizes the lease pre-check as `log_limit + 2 MiB`, which is 4 MiB at the default budget, as before.
- **Values** (`.github/server-active-captures.json`):

| Suite | `timeoutSeconds` | `logLimitBytes` | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture-shadow` | 1500 | 4 MiB | **measured**: 684.6 s + 45 s, about 2×; log measured under 2 MiB |
| `bridge-context-configured-runtime` | 1500 | 24 MiB | **estimated** from the measured rate (about 60 runtime tests × 7–10 s, plus 45 s) and 2 MiB per about 11 tests (projected about 11 MiB), about 2× |
| every other enrolled suite | 600 | 2 MiB | **estimated**: today's bounds for the whole run, now per suite; unit-level suites |

- **CI job:** `server-ut-st` `timeout-minutes` 25 → 90, for the expected total of about 45 min (per-suite overhead about 45 s × 22, plus the two long suites), doubled. The job stays paused (`if: false`, #1014).
- **Reviewed active identity:** `ACTIVE_SOURCE_SHA` in the `server-host-controls` bootstrap job now names this PR's first commit, which changes `server_active_output.py` and `server_active_entry.py`.

## Verification

- `tests/server/test_active_entry.py`, `test_active_output.py`, `test_active_owner_handoff.py`: **55 passed, 46 subtests**. `test_suite_manifest.py`'s reviewed-bound pin now checks the new ceilings and that the largest budget plus headroom fits the 128 MiB output tmpfs. New cases:
  - each suite runs in its own capture, in registry order, with its own bounds;
  - a failing suite stops the run and names itself;
  - bounds come only from the registry and stay within the reviewed ceilings;
  - `capture` refuses timeout or bytes above the ceilings;
  - the suite's budget reaches `capture` as `maximum`.
- All of `tests/server` (macOS, py3.13, excluding 4 modules that don't import in this venv): 873 passed, 13 failed, 35 errors. Main `14d284a6` in the same environment: 868 passed with the **identical** 13 failures and 35 errors (installed-package proof and composio tooling not present locally). **No new failures.**
- **Not yet done:** the per-suite proof on a native amd64 host. The HK cluster is at about 99% memory requested on both nodes, so the measurement Pod can't schedule. When capacity allows, I'll run this PR head as trusted base with #1575 as candidate, post the per-suite times and bytes here, and tighten the estimated values.

Local sandbox note (`DigitalMate-tools/server-ut-st-sandbox`): its stand-in hooks `execute`'s single `--suite all` and needs a matching update. That's a tool change, not part of this PR.

1641.author: Jianyu010
1641.body:
Fixes #1618

## What changes
A quick reply is written from the **committed** task view. While an earlier input of the same session has no committed normal turn (claimed, running or queued), that turn can still create or change tasks, so the view can be stale.

- **Pending state:** `HiveReplyOrdering.earlier_inputs_pending(scope, session_ref, before_seq)` reads `dm_hive_inputs` (user, status and done rows with a lower `seq` and no `consumed_at_ms`). `BeebouQuickRunner.snapshot(hedge=True)` then adds `[quick] pending_note` after the task view. It is not added to the secondary preparation.
- **Prompt clause:** `pending_note` tells the model not to say that a task, Bee, report, draft or queue is absent or empty, or what is in progress, and to say it is still setting it up.
- **Absence guard:** `review_quick_text(..., pending=True)` refuses (`QuickReplyRefused` code `absence_while_pending`, recorded by `refuse_quick_reply`) a candidate with one clause that names a roster or queue thing (`absence_subjects`) and an absence (`absence_markers`). A hedged text names no such pair and still publishes. Not pending: unchanged.
- **Stale running claim (FOLLOW-04 scope addition):** a clause that names a task and says it is still running (`running_claims`, Latin ones unless negated) is refused with `task_state_mismatch` when the task view the candidate was given holds no task in `active_task_states`, or while pending.
- All word lists, the note, the view prefix and the active states are in `quick_reply.toml`; nothing is hard-coded. The false-completion guard (#1437) is unchanged.

## FOLLOW-04 finding (which case it was)
In `HIVE-LIVE-FOLLOW-04/r2` the travel task completed at +124447 ms and T3 was sent at +127727 ms, 3.3 s later. T3's quick snapshot is read at admission, so its view already showed the task as completed (the pre-T3 Store snapshot says so); no earlier input was pending at T3 (T2's turn ended at +66 s). The model therefore **contradicted its input**: it repeated "still generating" from T2's committed answer. The trace holds no request bodies, so this is inferred from those timestamps, not read from the quick request. The `task_state_mismatch` guard covers this; `pending` does not apply to it.

## Tests (all enrolled)
- `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_quick_absence_pending.py`: the Codex controlled journey on the real CLI assembly, Gateway, Host, Store and runner. Defect cases `test_issue_p3_r2_roster_claim_is_refused` and `test_issue_qr_r1_empty_queue_claim_is_refused`; controls `test_control_a_hedged_quick_reply_still_publishes` and `test_control_a_false_completion_claim_is_still_refused`. Enrolled as extra `owner_tests` of SC03-B3.
- `temp/hive-beebou/tests/test_beebou_quick_reply.py`: guard on the shipped config (absence, still-running, hedge, negation, language) and the host-note and task-view wiring.
- `temp/hive-runtime/tests/test_hive_runtime_quick_runner.py`: the note appears only when pending and only for the quick view.
- `agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_quick_pending_input.py`: the Store read. `test_hive_quick_refusal.py`: FOLLOW-04 shape on the real Store and runner: a completed task while the quick reply says it is running is refused with `task_state_mismatch` and recorded REFUSED; the same text against a queued task publishes (the completion is a labelled Store-row update).

## Before / after
Codex repro `/private/tmp/hive-1618-controlled-808ebcd.gd6c24/run.sh /private/tmp/hive-1618-controlled-808ebcd.gd6c24/test_1618_controlled.py -k test_issue --tb=short`:

| | before (hive3 `780c7402`) | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| defect asserts | 2 failed (`QUICK_COMMITTED`, expected `refused`) | pass |
| controls (hedge, direct guard) | pass | pass |
| total | 2 failed, 2 passed | 4 passed |

| Suite | after |
| --- | --- |
| hive-beebou (`temp/hive-beebou/tests`) | 105 passed |
| hive-runtime (`temp/hive-runtime/tests`) | 98 passed |
| quick-reply scenarios (`test_phase2_quick_reply.py`, new journey) | 14 passed (new journey stable on 3 repeats) |
| bridge quick/capacity/tool-error tests | 54 passed |

Not caused by this change: `test_hive_runner.py::test_owner_test_helper_paths_are_appended_not_prepended` (depends on the `PYTHONPATH` order of my local run), PDF document tests and `test_phase2_bee_factory_observation.py` (the same PDF and factory tests fail on the untouched `780c7402` source in the same venv).

## Out of scope
Default steer changes, quick-path redesign, and the STEER-01 "added/delivered" wording while the steer is pending (separate post-cutover issue).

1649.body:
**Known limit: report generation fails closed until #1640.**

#1313 removed the legacy task executor that report turns ran on. `SessionManager.submit_event` now refuses every event, and the Bridge runs `EngineService(legacy_execution=False)`. This PR follows decision B: every report stage fails closed with a clear error that is not retried. It does not admit report turns into the person's Beebou Home conversation. Live memory ingestion reads that history into Global Memory, and re-enabling legacy execution would bypass G6's fence. Moving report generation onto Hive is tracked in #1640 (DM31-A07, v3.5). That issue also holds the discarded option-A patch, for reference only.

## Behaviour differences
- Every report stage (correlate, brief, revise, mail_update, ppt, edit_ppt) raises `ReportGenerationUnavailable`.
  - Code: `REPORT_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Message: "Report generation is unavailable in this build while it moves to Hive (DM31-A07)".
  - Both are constants in `dm_report_goals.store`.
- The failure is recorded as the goal's `processing_error` and the new `processing_error_code`.
  - A new goal ends `failed` at version 0, never stuck at `received` and never retried.
  - An existing plan keeps its version and plan.
  - A Retry is a new operation and fails the same way. There is no retry loop.
- Correlation with earlier reports counts as generation. It is skipped, and the new mail's goal fails closed.
- These still work: signal ingest (HTTP callback and `report.signal.ingest`), goals, cards, history, mail detail, operation lookup, and download of existing artifacts.
- No report turn reaches a model or the Beebou conversation. The tests assert that `dm_hive_inputs` stays empty.
- `report_runtime.SessionReportAgent.run` keeps its sandbox check and then fails closed. The `submit_event` body was removed.
- `ownership.json`:
  - The 3 new public symbols are exported.
  - `report-runtime-adapter` no longer declares the legacy imports of session-policy and session-proximity-admission.
- README: added a section on the current state on the Router-free Bridge and where report generation is going (DM31-A07).

## Tests (owner tests carry the #1313 reason)
- `test_report_http`: the 2 executor-backed tests are replaced by fail-closed owner tests: signal→failed, duplicate, list, stale update, and existing plan kept with revise and correlate failing closed. The callback auth test is kept.
- `test_report_ws`: the retry test now asserts that a retry fails closed again without a loop. The fixture moved to the Hive Home profile (`report_hive_fixture.py`, the real `configured_bridge` with Beebou, and a labelled CONTROLLED model server).
- `test_report_runtime`: added a test that every stage fails closed and a foreign sandbox is refused first.

## Counts
These come from the gate's own `load_registry`/`execute_suite` in `scripts/ci/server-tests.py`, run locally on a clean env. The full selector refuses candidate phases outside the protected runner.

| suite | base 780c7402 | head |

| report-goals | 38 tests, 2F, 2E, exit 1 | **39 tests, 0F, 0E, exit 0** (also after merging hive3 6cac213b) |

- The architecture/ownership/inventory checker (`tools/architecture/check.py`) is clean.

Client fixes from the device runs on candidate 6cac213b. Base: hive3 faf4aaab. Head: 07edcadf.

## 1. Attachments in the per-Bee composer (SC04-C1 single device)
The per-Bee composer had no attachment control, so "one device targets two Bees in turn, sending text and attachments" (docs/scenarios/hive-g5-plan.md:158) couldn't be done from the HAP.

**The wire already supports it.** #1603 `hive.message.send {message_id, text, target_session_ref, source_ids}` is accepted on the direct socket, and the Host routes the files with the text. The server half is agent_bridge `test_hive_session_target.py::test_single_device_journey_across_two_bees`.

- **`DigitalMateHiveNamedTextRequest`**: new optional `source_ids`.
- **`DigitalMateHiveSteerComposer`**: per-lane draft attachments.
  - They go only on the named send.
  - A pending retry resends the same `message_id` with the original IDs.
  - Acceptance clears them; a refusal keeps them.
  - They are locked while a send is unresolved.
  - Text-only steer, queue and preempt don't send while files are attached.
- **`HiveActivityPanel`**: new 添加附件 button (only with a named target) and file chips.
- **`Index.ets`**: uploads to the Home room using the Home composer's picker, validation and upload socket, and queues removal of dropped uploads.

## 2. No `hive.bee.stop {}` probe
On every open and reconnect, the page probed `hive.bee.stop {}`, and the server logged a ValueError each time.
- Stop now follows the snapshot's `busy_controls.stop`; only `hive.result.get` is probed.

1652.author: Jianyu010
1652.body:
G5 blocker: a targeted Bee run stays RUNNING forever when the runtime ends with an empty `chat.final` (candidate 6cac213b, SC04-C1 step 1, alpha run_9ce80c4f).

## Cause
`text_run` reports a final without text as `unresolved`. `run_next` returned that without settling the Run, so the Run stayed RUNNING, the Bee input was never consumed and the Bee lane stayed blocked. A stream that ended with its final only on the reasoning channel raised `RuntimeError` in `stream_bound_bee`, with the same effect.

## Fix (no identity-hashed Harness code changed)
- `workswarm_adapter.stream_bound_bee`: a turn with no final answer still waits for the runtime's own completion observation. Without that proof it still raises.
- `bee_runtime.run_turn`: keeps the Host evidence of an `unresolved` turn whose lane saw its completion.
- `HostBeeCompletionVerifier.verify_empty_terminal`: a witness only from a fresh COMPLETED proof of the exact request, a clean Host execution and the Store's current claim.
- `BeeExecutionBridge._fail_empty_terminal` (new run and queued supplement): `commit_failed_turn(reason="empty_final")` ends the Run, fails the task with its notice and settles the task's inputs (`consume_kind='settled'`) in one commit, after the Store commit. The Bee is idle again.
- The failed frame now carries `reason`, with `text: ""`. Reasoning is never promoted into a reply. Without the proof the claim stays RUNNING as before.

## Observed shape (device run_9ce80c4f, deploy lane evidence)
The runtime finished normally in 4.4 s with `chat.final` `content: ""` and the model's SVG in `reasoning_content`, then `chat.usage_summary`; no tool call. That is the empty-answer path above. Store left behind: task `running`, Run RUNNING, input seq 7 unconsumed, no failed/stopped/unavailable row.

## What stays RUNNING by design (no fresh COMPLETED proof)
If the runtime cannot show a COMPLETED proof for the exact request (stream error, restart, evicted Session, UNKNOWN/BUSY/FAILED/STALE after the bounded retries, mismatched generation), no witness is issued and the claim stays RUNNING, as for every other turn without a witness. **No existing path ends that case**:
- #1611's unavailable terminal covers only queued, never-claimed tasks whose Session binding conflicts; an entered Run is never covered.
- `resume_running` returns `unresolved` for an entered claim with no durable queue head, and there is no timeout or restart reconciliation that settles it.

So an orphaned RUNNING Run remains possible; this PR narrows it to "the runtime cannot prove it finished". Restart recovery of orphaned Runs is tracked in #1655.

## What the device user sees for `empty_final`
- **Frame:** `digitalmate.task.text` for that task and Run with `state: "failed"`, `final: true`, `text: ""`, `reason: "empty_final"`. It carries one `event_id` from the Store notice, so it is delivered and deduplicated like any terminal. It is the same frame as the #1547 failed terminal, plus `reason`.
- **Where:** the Bee's lane for that task. The pending state ("发送结果待确认" / "Bee 正在处理") ends, because the task is `failed`, the Run ENDED and the input consumed. The Bee takes the next targeted message.
- **Wording:** this PR authors no user-facing sentence. The server sends no text, only `state` and `reason`. How the client words a failed task with empty text is client-side. `reason` lets it word an empty reply differently from other failures, and I have not checked the device client's rendering. If it shows nothing for an empty failed frame, that needs a client change.

## Before / after (`tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_bee_empty_final.py`, real Store/Registry/Host/verifier/adapter, controlled WorkSwarm wire)
- Before: `run_next` returns `unresolved`; Run RUNNING, input unconsumed.
- After: `failed`, Run ENDED with an empty-terminal witness, task failed, one notice, input settled once, the reasoning text appears nowhere in the Store, and the next targeted message to the same Bee is claimed and answered ("2+3" gives "5"). Reasoning-channel-only final: same. No completion proof: stays RUNNING.
- Enrolled as owner tests of SC04-C1.

Local: new tests 4/4; `test_phase2_bee_verifier`, bridge `test_hive_bee_*`, `test_workswarm_adapter`, hive-runtime/worker/beebou tests and scenarios pass. Known pre-existing failures: `test_phase2_bee_factory_observation` (3), and `test_hive_runner` path order under my local PYTHONPATH.

Not covered: a Run already stuck RUNNING (alpha run_9ce80c4f) is not recovered by this change; it needs a reconcile or a fresh run. A queued-supplement empty final uses the same code path but has no dedicated test.

1676.body:
## Summary

Re-lands #1601 on `main` after the Router-retirement cutover, per the operator's instruction on that PR.
Tracks #1673; collected under #1665 (post-HIVE non-blocking items) and #1344.

`main` was at `498bc351` (merge of #1605). Git already records #1601's commits as merged, so the original
branch had an empty diff against `main`; this branch re-applies the change the only way that produces a
real diff — by reverting the revert:

- `5eff0b11` `Reapply "Merge pull request #1601…"` (inverse of `47e5a102`), applied with **no conflicts**
- `c7032640` records the re-land branch and its verification numbers in `TRACEABILITY.md`

23 files, +3298 / −49. The tree equals the reviewed head `d5d338e4` (second review round included) on top
of the post-cutover `main`.

## What it does

`temp/hive-trust/` — a read-only diagnostics partition: correlated, token-validated events with explicit
`AUTHORITATIVE` / `OBSERVATION` / `CLIENT_DISPLAY` evidence kinds, a conservative "where did this request
stop?" investigator (`NoReplyInvestigator`, `investigate_message`, `investigate_delivery`), and a passive
recorder that never changes an owner's outcome. Emitters sit at the real owner boundaries of the Beebou
turn path:

| Owner boundary | Events |
| --- | --- |
| `server_engine/hive_turn_startup.py` `accept` | `message.received`, `admission.result` |
| `DiagnosticReceiver` around `AdmissionReceiver` | `dispatch.started`, `dispatch.receipt`, `dispatch.result` |
| `hive_turn_startup.py` `run_input` / `_record_turn_result` | `beebou.started`, `beebou.result`, `result.committed` |
| `hive_turn_startup.py` `_publish` | `output.attempt`, `output.result` |
| `hive_beebou_model.py` | `model.started`, `model.result` |
| `hive_beebou_tools.py` | `tool.started`, `tool.result` |

Behaviour is opt-in and inert by default: `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_DIAGNOSTICS` absent or `off` installs no
recorder (`configured_recorder` returns `None`), every emitter is a no-op, and any other value refuses
startup instead of silently collecting nothing. No existing public interface changes.

Packaging and ownership travel with it: Bridge wheel force-include, `.github/ci-gates.json`
`sourcePaths`/`sourcePackages`, `scripts/ci/server_context_source.py`, `temp/hive-beebou/ownership.json`
(`hive-trust-diagnostics` in `allowed`, `legacy-mobile-gateway` admitted as caller),
`temp/hive-trust/ownership.json`, and the installed-package proof rows.

## Review findings

#1601's two review rounds are fully applied here: F1–F8 (first round) and R1–R8 (second round, table in
[this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/DigitalMate/pull/1601#issuecomment-6909293212)).
Each fix has a test that failed on the previous behaviour first. Per-finding tables, line-level code trace
and dispositions (including the one documented gate gap: the suite is pytest-style while the enrolled CI
gate discovers with `unittest`, so enrolling it would select zero tests) are in
`temp/hive-trust/TRACEABILITY.md`.

## Relationship to the trust items in #1665

This layer is the evidence path those items need; it does not fix them:

- **#1637 (STEER-01)** — a reply claims a steer was added while its receipt is pending/unconsumed. The
  evidence kinds here are exactly the separation between "the owner admitted it" and "a reply claims it".
- **#1650** — relayed Bee results missing from the Home transcript. Display is only proven by
  `CLIENT_DISPLAY`, which has no producer yet (see follow-ups).
- **#1653** — a turn settling as a generic failure although the Bee got the task. The investigator reports
  `UNKNOWN` with the missing fact and the next owner instead of a generic failure.
- **#1655** — orphaned `RUNNING` Bee Runs. Correlation by message / delivery / task ref is what a recovery
  walk uses to find them.
- **#1663** — the device receipt runner must enforce each row's required steps. Same rule here: a row
  without its named evidence is `NOT_RUN`, never a pass.

## Verification (this branch)

```text
pytest temp/hive-trust/tests -q
52 passed

pytest temp/hive-beebou/tests tests/architecture/test_import_gate.py -q
111 passed, 29 subtests passed

python tools/architecture/transition.py --check docs/implementations/migration/module-ownership.json --root .
exit 0 — hive-trust: 2 components, 0 adapters
```

The emitters are exercised by tests that drive real owners: `deliver` over a real `AdmissionReceiver` and
`SQLiteSessionRepository`, a commit cut off by the attempt deadline, another message's receipt (replay
cache), a malformed tool call, real `HiveTurnStartup.accept`, a controlled model gateway, a faulting tool
provider, failing/succeeding push callables, concurrent turns, unsafe identifiers and a failing sink.

## Honest coverage

`T01` (lost admission ACK against the real Store) and `D01–D05` are PASS at the owner-boundary level.

**`T02`, `T04–T80`, `C01–C24` and `H01–H08` are NOT_RUN.** They need producers, devices, real models or
Host grants this change does not provide. Plan §6.2 rows 2 (Inbox enqueue+claim), 5 (Bee
activation/run/state), 8 (recovery) and `decision.result` / `quick_reply.result` / `interaction.state` are
not instrumented. Nothing here may be read as coverage for them.

## Environment limits (not fixed, not claimed)

- The Bridge's declared runtime dependencies are not installed on this host. `telethon==1.45.0`,
  `zstandard>=0.23,<1` and `icalendar>=7.3,<8` (`pyproject.toml:37`, `:43`, `:20`) were missing, so the
  files that import the connectors did not collect at all. Installing those three into a throwaway
  directory and putting `agent_bridge/tests` and `tests/scenarios/hive` on `PYTHONPATH` clears it: the
  Beebou/turn-startup files now run **96 passed**, `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase3_client_payloads.py`
  runs **6 passed**, and `tests/scenarios/hive` collects **386 tests, 0 collection errors**. This is a
  host-dependency fact, not a property of the change; the collected scenarios have not been run in full,
  and no scenario result is claimed here.
- `tests/scenarios/run_hive.py --prepare-deps` does not terminate on Windows: `prepare_dependencies`
  (`run_hive.py:134`) looks for `DIR/bin/python`, which a Windows venv never creates
  (`Scripts/python.exe`), so the documented unblock cannot be used on this host; the three packages were
  installed by hand instead.
- `jiuwenswarm` (the WorkSwarm Bee runtime) is not installed, so G5/G6 and the scenarios that drive it
  cannot run here.
- `tests/server/test_installed_package_proof.py`: 4 failures are `os.symlink` `WinError 1314` on this host
  and 23 errors are the bundled `pip` bootstrap `ssl.SSLError`; the admission/registry assertions for
  `hive-trust` pass. The LF byte pins only match on a checkout without `core.autocrlf`.
- Symlink-dependent tests fail with `WinError 1314`.
- Cloud deployment / real-phone validation is **NOT_RUN**; the planned end-to-end path is written in
  #1673 (run `tests/scenarios/run_hive.py --gate G1`, then one test-env deployment with
  `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_DIAGNOSTICS=log` over the four fault cases).

No real credentials, accounts, devices, models, databases or external side effects were used; all Store
instances are temporary and synthetic.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs, deliberately not here)

1. A `CLIENT_DISPLAY` producer from the client, without which no diagnosis can reach `COMPLETED` on a
   real device.
2. A reader that parses `hive_diag` log lines back into events, so end-to-end reconciliation is automatic.
3. Instrumenting plan §6.2 rows 2, 5, 8 with their owners.

## Migration

The partition stays read-only and temporary. Move it into the reviewed observability owner once that owner
publishes the event schema and query interface; keep emitters only at commit/observation boundaries, and
delete the partition after the owner's tests cover lost ACK, no-reply, committed-but-undisplayed and
unknown-dependency behaviour.

Closes #1673.

1677.body:
Fixes #1670 (P0, the only G5 FAIL at cutover: SC04-C1 C1-S1, the attachment half).

## Root cause
The attachment reached the Bee's Store input row intact. Seq 7 carries `source_ids [message_id, attachment-…]`. The Host then dropped it while reading that row. `DeliveredInput` (`session_proximity/hive_store.py`) had no `source_ids`, and `read_delivered_input` did not select the column. So `BeeHostExecution.run_turn` could only give the Bee runtime `message.text`. There was also no read path: the owned Bee runs ask-only, with no native file tool.

The `delivery/messages.py` "native queue cannot carry an attachment" error belongs to the Home queue path, not this route. It is unchanged; the bot review on #1670 says the same.

## Fix
- **Store owner read:** `DeliveredInput.source_ids` comes from `read_delivered_input` (a new field with a default; no schema change).
- **Attachment owner:** `Attachments.read_bee_input_source(scope, source_id)` rechecks the scope and principal, the source's active state and visibility, and the stored bytes against the size and sha256 recorded at upload. The input row is a reference, never authority.
- **Host materializer** (`temp/hive-runtime/.../assembly/bee_input_sources.py`): `BeeHostExecution.run_turn` calls it after the entry fence and before the Harness. That covers the claimed first input and every queued supplement, since `_drain_queue` uses the same `run_turn`. For each id that matches `[sources] attachment_id_pattern`, it:
  - copies the bytes atomically to `<Bee runtime home>/hive-inputs/<sha256(task_ref)>/<source_id>/<name>` (0700, linked folders refused, unsafe names fall back to the source id);
  - checks the copy's sha256 and size again;
  - adds the path to the turn text, plus the content for `text/plain` and `text/markdown`, fenced as source data.

  Other ids are message lineage and are ignored.
- **Fails visibly:** a source that is unavailable (missing, revoked, foreign), over a limit (`too_large`, `too_many`), or fails a check (`integrity`, `copy_failed`) is named in the turn as `NOT delivered (<reason>)`, so the Bee tells the user. It is also logged. Nothing is dropped silently.
- **Config, not code:** `dm_hive_runtime/config/bee_input_sources.toml` holds the id pattern, `max_count`, `max_source_bytes`, `max_input_bytes`, the folder name, the inline media types, `max_chars` and all turn wording.
- **Wiring:** the product Bridge passes `self.engine.attachments` to `compose_bee_runtime(..., input_sources=...)`.
- `ownership.json` registers the new public names. The architecture scan reports no findings: 266 files checked.

## Decisions (recorded in `beebou-hive-phase3-delivery.md` §7a and `contracts/UPDATES.md`)
- **Mechanism:** the Host copies the file into the Bee's per-Task input folder and puts the path and text in the turn. No new tool grant. With effects off (the device setup), the turn is the only way an ask-only Bee can read a file.
- **Not behind `[documents] model_reads`:** a user's explicit attachment to a Bee is user input, the same as a manager turn's text attachment. Withdrawal before the turn is fenced by the owner recheck at turn start.
- **Known limits (follow-ups under #1665):**
  - Binary types (PDF, images, Office) get only the path. Reading them should share #1640's reader.
  - The Attachment owner's erasure does not yet remove the Host copy under `hive-inputs/`.
  - Admission still checks `source_ids` for shape only. The read-time owner check is the authority.
  - Text already delivered stays in the Bee Session, as the #1602 row says.

## Tests
- `harness/.../tests/test_hive_bee_input_sources.py` runs on the real path: CLI `configured_bridge` WebSocket `hive.message.send` routing, the real Engine Attachment owner, the Hive Store, the Registry, `compose_bee_runtime`/`BeeHostExecution.run_turn`, the Host verifier, `BeeExecutionBridge` with its queue drain, and the `WorkSwarmAdapter` text run. Controlled (labelled): the model that creates the two Bees, and the WorkSwarm wire.
  - First input: the file is in the Bee's per-Task folder with byte-identical content and a matching sha256. The runtime turn (`chat.send` content) carries its path, size, sha256 and text. The committed Bee context equals that turn.
  - Queued supplement: an attachment sent as a steer while the Bee's turn is held in the runtime reaches the supplement turn the same way.
  - Negative: a never-uploaded id and a revoked source are each named `NOT delivered (unavailable)`, with no copy and no withdrawn text in the turn. An available source beside them is still delivered.
  - Without the `run_turn` hook all three fail.
- `temp/hive-runtime/tests/test_hive_runtime_input_sources.py` (enrolled pattern) covers lineage-only input, inline vs path-only, replay, `too_large`/`too_many`, digest mismatch, no owner or home, linked folder, unsafe name, truncation and settings validation.
- Enrolled as SC04-C1 owner tests in `tests/scenarios/hive/assertions.toml`. SC04-C1's owner tests used to stop at the input row.

Local run on head `c64ddacc` (Python 3.13.13 with the CI constraints and `openjiuwen`, macOS):
- Bridge `tests/test_hive_*.py`, `test_engine_attachments.py`, `test_workswarm_adapter.py`, `test_workswarm_bee_effects.py`: **518 passed**, 5 skipped, 7 xfailed.
- `temp/hive-runtime`, `temp/hive-worker`, `temp/hive-beebou` tests: **317 passed**.
- Hive scenarios (`test_phase2_bee_*`, `test_phase3_bee_*`, text flow, queue fence, busy gateway, bound Bee, runtime binding, `test_home_bee_*`): **168 passed**, 41 skipped. The 3 failures are in `test_phase2_bee_factory_observation` (AF_UNIX path too long / launcher check under my scratchpad venv). The same 3 fail on unchanged `main` `498bc351` in the same environment.
- `tests/scenarios/test_hive_runner.py` registry checks: 25 passed.
- Not run: the WorkSwarm-runtime-gated tests (`WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`) and the full CI matrix.

## Remaining acceptance step
**A device rerun of SC04-C1 S1** (per-Bee composer 添加附件 → the Bee reads the file) is out of reach here and is the remaining acceptance step. Expect the turn to show "Attached files, delivered by the Host" with the path, and the Bee to quote the `.txt` content.

1681.author: Jianyu010
1681.body:
Closes #1655.

A Bee Run the Host had entered could stay `RUNNING` forever after a restart or a missing terminal. Its input stayed unconsumed and its Bee lane stayed blocked. This PR settles such a Run only on Host evidence, never on a timer.

## Decisions (contract §7c)

| | Decision |
|---|---|
| F1 isolation witness | At entry, in the same transaction as the ENTERED flip, the Store records the owned runtime instance (`<host boot uuid>:<child pid>`). After the turn it records the runtime session, request and generation (`dm_hive_bee_run_runtimes`). A Run settles only on (a) the runtime's fresh proof for the recorded session, or (b) proof that the recorded runtime is gone: a different instance, a different pid, and the recorded process dead (`os.kill(pid, 0)` → `ProcessLookupError`, POSIX only). Without either, the Run stays `RUNNING` with a WARNING diagnostic. `bee_execution.toml [orphan_recovery] recheck_interval_ms` only paces re-checks. |
| F2 committed context, no head | The committed context's text is delivered once as the normal text terminal. The `interrupted` failed-turn commit is used only when no context was committed. |
| F3 orphan predicate | `RUNNING`, entry fence `ENTERED`, no Stop or preempt reservation, no `OPEN` question, no answered-but-undelivered answer, no `PLANNED` effect. A `CLAIMED` queued supplement settles through its own `queue:<seq>` turn. `commit_failed_turn(orphan=True)` re-checks the predicate inside its transaction. |
| F4 client | No client code here. The doc records the server frame and what the client renders today. The real gap is split out to #1678, a sub-issue of #1665. |
| F5 | The predecessor chain is fixed to #1496 → #1547 → #1652. Scope-2 test: an empty final on a queued supplement's `queue:<seq>` turn ends the task failed once. |

## Changes
- `hive_busy.py`: new table `dm_hive_bee_run_runtimes`, plus `record_bee_run_runtime`, `read_bee_run_runtime` and `read_orphaned_turn`. `enter_bee_run` takes `turn` and `runtime`. New `BeeRunRuntime` and `OrphanTurn` types, listed in module-ownership.json.
- `bee_runtime.py` / `bee_verifier.py`: the owned runtime instance, the post-turn runtime record, and `verify_orphan` with the witness rules above. The `WorkSwarmBeeHarness` methods that feed the implementation identity are unchanged.
- `hive_bee_execution.py` / `hive_bee_scheduler.py` / `server.py`: `resume_running` → `_recover_orphan` on both the no-head and head paths.
- Config: `[orphan_recovery] recheck_interval_ms = 30000`.

1689.body:
Refs #1650 (stays open until the device receipt: relay visible in Home live and after reload). Tracked under #1665 (post-HIVE) and #1533's G5 Home requirement: Beebou "delivers its result" in Home.

## Root cause
A Bee's result reaches Beebou as a `kind='done'` input (`sender_ns='bot:<bee>'`, `role=EVENT`). Beebou's relay of it was already committed in `dm_hive_beebou_context_runs` under that input's seq. But all four Home reads in `hive_store.py` (`list_beebou_home_submissions`, `beebou_home_message_position` and the two `beebou_home_message_page` queries) filtered on `sender_ns='user' AND kind='user' AND role=USER`. So the relay never reached Home: not live, and not after a reload. The client used the live `hive.beebou.reply {trigger:'bee_done'}` push only as an Activity refresh trigger.

## Fix
**Server (Store owner read, no schema change)**
- The four reads now share one `_HOME_SUBMISSIONS` query. It still admits the principal's inputs as before. It also admits a `done` input when all of these hold: the sender is a Bee (`bot:<author_bot_id>`, `author_role='bee'`, `role=EVENT`), the input is on the active Beebou binding, and its relay is `COMPLETED` with a non-empty answer.
- A done row is **reply-only**:
  - Its `text` is selected as `''`, so the Bee's report text never reaches Home.
  - `_HOME_MESSAGES` emits no `user` part for it, so there is no phantom `:user` message, position or cursor. A cursor on one is `BAD_PARAMS`.
  - `f.notice` is kept for user rows only. A failed or uncommitted relay shows nothing.
- `BeebouHomeSubmission.relay_bee_id` (new field with a default) marks the row.
- `home_messages` (`temp/hive-beebou`) renders a relay as `hive-home:<session>:<seq>:reply`, with `kind: result`, `trigger: bee_done` and `bee_id`. It is placed by consume time, like any reply. `hive_home_trial.py` is **unchanged**: `_history_position` and `_mixed_history_page` already pick the reply view for a reply part.
- A relay can be quoted like any Beebou reply: `_home_reply_text` resolves a committed relay too. Before this change, the quote button on the new bubble would have been refused with `SOURCE_FORBIDDEN`.

**Client (ArkTS)**
- `DigitalMateConversation.acceptHiveRelay(event)` takes a committed, final, non-empty `hive.beebou.reply {trigger: bee_done}` for the open Home. It adds the relay as a stored row under the durable ID `hive-home:<session_ref>:<source_seq>:reply`. Both fields are already in the push.
- The model merges rows by ID, so the later snapshot or history row replaces it (same pattern as `mergeHistory`). This gives one bubble whichever arrives first, and a replayed push adds nothing.
- `DigitalMateHome/Index.ets` calls it on the push, renders, and schedules a refresh.
- `DigitalMateProtocol.ets`: optional `trigger`/`bee_id` on messages. Also optional `trigger`, `outcome`, `bot_id`, `bee_id`, `session_ref` and `source_seq` on events (these fields were already on the wire).

**Docs:** the #1650 row in `beebou-hive-phase3-delivery.md` §7a changes from "known limit" to the projected behaviour. `temp/hive-beebou/home-trial.md` now notes relays.

## Tests
**Server.** `harness/.../tests/test_hive_home_relays.py` (matches `test_hive_*.py`; enrolled under SC04-C1 in `tests/scenarios/hive/assertions.toml`) runs on the real path: CLI `configured_bridge`/`create_app` WebSocket Home (`room.home`, `room.message`, `task.create`, `room.messages`, `snapshot`), the SQLite Hive Store, BotTools report and the HiveBusy terminal commit. Controlled participants (labelled): the model HTTP server and the Bee runtime from `test_hive_bee_induced_reply` (claim, done report, Host commit).
- Before the terminal commit, the done input changes nothing in Home. After it, the live push's `(session_ref, source_seq)` ID equals the projected row's ID. The row has the exact shape above, it is last in order, and there is no `:user` row and no Bee text.
- After a follow-up turn, the order is user, reply, **relay**, user, reply. Quoting the relay is accepted, and the model receives the relay text as `quoted_reply`.
- Paging two at a time reaches every row once, in order. A cursor on the relay returns the rows before it. A cursor on the phantom `:user` ID is `BAD_PARAMS`.
- **After a reload** (a new Bridge on the same Store): the same snapshot rows and the same history page, with no model call.
- If a pending user input runs before an earlier-admitted `done` (lower seq), the relay is still placed after that user turn's reply, in the snapshot and in history. The direct Store read returns it reply-only.
- Without the server change both tests fail (`not enough values to unpack`, and the projected ID mismatch).

**Client.**
- `hive_home_relay_model.mjs` runs the **HAP's ArkTS `DigitalMateConversation`** under Node against the captured server payloads. It checks one bubble in both orders (push then snapshot, snapshot then push), a replayed push, parity with the reload, that the relay is quotable, and that failed, partial, user-triggered, malformed and other-room pushes are refused.
- `digitalmate/entry/src/test/HiveHomeRelays.test.ets` (hypium, registered in `List.test.ets`) covers the same three cases on device-shaped data.

**Local runs** (macOS, Python 3.13.13 scratch venv with `PYTHONPATH` on this tree; DevEco hvigor):
- Rebased head `2fc92e4f` on `c5a4f30b`: bridge `tests/test_hive_*.py` **434 passed**, 3 skipped, 7 xfailed. `tests/scenarios/test_hive_runner.py` **41 passed**.
- Pre-rebase head: bridge `tests/test_hive_*.py` + `tests/test_session_proximity*.py` gave 878 passed, 12 failed. The 12 are in `test_session_proximity_{a01_consumer,legacy_receipts,acceptance,integration}`. The **same 12 fail on unchanged `498bc351`** in the same environment. `temp/hive-beebou` + `temp/hive-runtime` tests: **203 passed**.
- Client: `hvigorw test -p module=entry@default -p testType=unit`: **BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 2334 tests, 0 failures**, including the 3 `hiveHomeRelays` cases. Its coverage post-step logged `getInitCoverageData failed` (JSON parse); the build and test result were not affected.
- Not run: the full CI matrix, and the HAP on a device.

## Remaining acceptance step
**Device receipt:** on the emulator against a deployed server, dispatch a Bee from Home and let it finish. Beebou's relay should appear in Home **live** (one bubble) and stay in place **after a reload**.

## Notes and follow-ups
- The relay takes one of the snapshot's 100 newest submissions (retained mode: the history window). Older turns stay reachable by paging.
- The live row stays in the model's local history until the room is reselected. If a Home context reset drops the session's rows, it could linger until then.
- The Activity Beebou lane (`activity_history`) still lists only user turns. Bee results stay in each Bee's lane. Not changed here.
- Sibling lanes are untouched: no edits to `hive_home_trial.py`, `server.py`, `hive_busy*.py`, `hive_bee_execution.py` or `hive_beebou_tools.py`.

## What changes
**#1637 (pending steer reported as applied).** `dispatch` results now carry a `detail` the model reads:
- a steer receipt with `delivery_state=pending` (no consumption witness): "Accepted, queued for the task, not yet applied … say it was passed on and will be picked up. Do not say it was added, applied or already included";
- an accepted `new`: queued, not yet started or applied.

The `dispatch` tool description states the rule: "added/applied" needs a later receipt or report showing the Bee consumed it. The normal turn has no persona prompt, so tool description plus result are the prompt surface. The pattern matches #1618/#1537: Host facts decide the wording. (`selection.py`, `hive_beebou_tools.py` addressed path)

**#1654 (steer of the task this turn just created).** Enforced in the Hive Host dispatch guard (the per-turn `HiveBeebouTools`). It remembers the `task_ref` of each accepted `new` of the turn and refuses a later steer of one before any Store write: `{"status":"refused","reason":"self_steer_same_turn","hint":"this task was created in this turn; put everything in the new task's text or answer the user"}`. It is a normal tool result (no tool-error budget used), writes no input/supplement/receipt and uses no steer quota. Steers of earlier-turn tasks, queued or running, are accepted as before (contract §6 matrix). The Store `_finish_steer` and the Delivery `FailureCode` vocabulary are unchanged. A line in the dispatch tool description says the same. Decision recorded in `docs/implementations/contracts/beebou-delivery-design.md` (§6).

## Evidence (rebased on origin/main 1e194a861)
Real SQLite Store + Bot Repository + Delivery + NativeBeebouRunner + Beebou Harness + Host provider; only the model is scripted. `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_beebou_steer_claims.py` (enrolled in SC03-B8):
- `test_same_turn_new_then_steer_is_refused_with_no_store_write_and_no_quota_use`: refusal; fingerprint of every non-Host `dm_hive_*` table identical before and after the call; no steer row; then `steers_per_task` (16) steers in later turns are all accepted and the 17th is `queue_full` (control).

Refs #1640 (part 1 of 2; part 2 adds ppt/edit_ppt and carries `Fixes #1640`).

## What
On the Router-free Bridge every mail-report stage failed with `REPORT_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` (re-verified on main `1e194a86`). Following the coordinator decision (Option 1), each report turn now runs as **one Host-admitted task of the person's Host-only report Bee**, with no Beebou model call. Part 1 runs the JSON stages: correlate, brief, revise and mail_update.

| Owner | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Bot Repository (`temp/hive-worker`) | `host_only` template flag. The new `report` template is not in `bee_templates()`, needs `register(host=True)`, stays out of `list_roster` (so out of `list_bees`, routing, create_bee reuse and the Bee scheduler), and never moves the roster version. |
| Hive Store (`hive_store.py`) | `activate_host_bee` (slotless; purpose fixed in the new `dm_hive_host_bees`), `admit_host_task` (dispatcher `host:<purpose>`; replay by message ID; `id_conflict` on another intent; `queue_full` not persisted) and `read_host_task`. A bot NewTask or SteerTask to a Host Bee is refused `target_not_found`. |
| Hive busy (`hive_busy.py`) | `list_unpublished_notices` skips Host-dispatched tasks, so a report result is never pushed to the person's clients. The notice obligation row is kept. |
| report-goals | `dm_report_goals.hive` holds the task text, identities, evidence file, result parsing and error codes. `config/report_bee.toml` holds every tunable. |
| `report_runtime` / `report_http` / `server.py` | The agent provisions the report Bee, uploads the evidence through the Attachment owner as a file input, admits under `hive-report-v1:<sha256(request_id)>`, drives the report Bee's lane with the Bridge's `BeeExecutionBridge`, and stops a Bee question. `Bridge.report_hive()` hands the owners to `mount_reports`. |

**Error mapping.**
- `RuntimeError`: a retryable admission state (`queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unknown`), an activation that is pending or unknown, or a timeout. The operation stays pending and is retried with the same request ID.
- `ReportTaskError` (a `ModelResultError`, so a `ValueError`): a refused admission, a failed or stopped task, or an unusable result. The codes are `REPORT_ADMISSION_REJECTED`, `REPORT_TASK_FAILED`, `REPORT_TASK_STOPPED` and `REPORT_RESULT_INVALID`, and the error is final for that operation.
- A Bridge without a Bee runtime keeps `REPORT_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE`.
- ppt and edit_ppt end with `REPORT_DECK_UNAVAILABLE` until part 2.

**Design.**
- Spec: `docs/implementations/contracts/hive-report-bee-v1.md` (RB-D1..D11, RB-S1..S8), plus an architecture-change review deck `hive-report-bee-v1.pptx`.
- The §7a rows were added or updated in `beebou-hive-phase3-delivery.md`.

It exercises the report HTTP routes, the ReportGoals worker, the Bot Repository, the Hive Store, the Attachment owner and Bee input materialization, the Host Bee execution and verifier, `BeeExecutionBridge` and `WorkSwarmAdapter`. Two participants are CONTROLLED: the WorkSwarm wire answering each Bee turn, and the Beebou model, which must never be called. The tests prove:
  - brief → revise → correlate → mail_update run as `host:report` tasks of one report Bee, with the evidence file inlined;
  - `conversation_ref` is `hive-report:<goal_id>`;
  - the Beebou model and Beebou inputs are untouched, there are no `user` inputs (memory ingestion), and no notice is pushed;
  - the roster and template list exclude the report Bee;
  - a replay reuses its task without a second Bee turn;
  - the retryable and final error mappings hold;
  - the PPTX stages write nothing.
- `harness/.../tests/test_hive_host_bee_store.py` (new, 4 tests): activation is slotless and idempotent, the purpose is fixed, admission replays or conflicts, `queue_full` is not persisted, and Beebou cannot dispatch to the report Bee.

1696.author: Jianyu010
1696.body:
Fixes #1640 (part 2 of 2). **Stacked on #1695.** This branch includes #1695's two commits until #1695 merges. The new change is the last commit, `3fc56545d`.

## What
Part 1 (#1695) ran correlate, brief, revise and mail_update on the Host-only report Bee. ppt and edit_ppt ended with `REPORT_DECK_UNAVAILABLE`. This PR runs those two stages on the same report Bee.

**How a deck is made.**
- ppt and edit_ppt are Host-admitted `host:report` tasks, like the JSON stages.
- The Bee returns slide JSON, `{"slides":[{"title","bullets"}]}`. `report_bee.toml [deck]` sets `max_slides`, `max_bullets` and `max_text_chars`.
- The Host renders the PPTX with `office_documents.generate_office_bytes` and `validate_office_bytes`.
- The Host stores the deck once per task through the Hive document byte owner (`HiveDocumentBytes.put`, operation `report-deck:<task_ref>`, request digest = slide digest).
- The goal artifact is `{artifact_ref, task_id: <host:report task>, mime_type, name, document: <byte receipt>[, source_artifact_ref]}`.

**Why the Host renders.** Bee document tools are an environment-gated effects-mode trial. Rendering on the Host gives every report deck one path that needs no grant, and the byte owner stays the only writer (RB-D12).

**edit_ppt.**
- The prior deck travels as a file input (`待修改报告.pptx`, path only).
- Its Host-extracted page-by-page text travels as a text input (`待修改报告内容.txt`, inlined), because the owned Bee has no native file tool.
- The new deck records `source_artifact_ref`, and the earlier deck is kept.

**Download.** `GET /internal/v1/report-goals/{goal}/artifacts/{ref}` reads a report-Bee deck back through `HiveDocumentBytes.read`, which rechecks scope, size and digest. Legacy artifacts still go through `artifact.read`.

**Errors (all final `ReportTaskError`).**
- `REPORT_PRIOR_DECK_UNAVAILABLE`: no deck on the goal, a receipt the byte owner refuses, an unreadable legacy artifact, or a non-PPTX payload. It is raised before admission, so nothing reaches the Bee.
- `REPORT_RESULT_INVALID`: an empty or unusable slide result.
- `REPORT_DECK_UNAVAILABLE` is removed.

**Replay.** A replayed deck turn reuses its task. The same operation then returns the same byte receipt, with no second Bee turn.

**Ownership.**
- `report-runtime-adapter` is allowed `bee-artifacts-hive-document-bytes` and gets legacy imports `office_documents.generate_office_bytes` and `validate_office_bytes`.
- `report-http-adapter` is allowed `bee-artifacts-hive-document-bytes`.
- New public symbols in `dm_report_goals.hive`: `prior_artifact`, `deck_slides`, `deck_digest`, `deck_result`, `REPORT_PRIOR_DECK_UNAVAILABLE`.

**Docs.**
- Spec `hive-report-bee-v1.md` is now "v1 implemented", with RB-D12/D13 and RB-S8..S10.
- Also updated: the §7a row in `beebou-hive-phase3-delivery.md`, the contracts README and `temp/report-goals/README.md`.
- The report-goals gate minimum rises from 42 to 47 (47 collected).

## Evidence (local, Python 3.13 venv)
- `temp/report-goals/tests/test_report_bee.py` has 8 tests on the real `configured_bridge(hive_bees=True)`/`create_app` path. CONTROLLED: the WorkSwarm wire answering each Bee turn. The Beebou model must never be called.
  - `test_ppt_and_edit_ppt_render_the_report_bees_slides_with_provenance` (RB-S8). Over HTTP `report.goal.confirm`:
    - ppt makes a ready goal with a PPTX artifact on a completed `host:report` task.
    - The download's slide titles match the Bee's slides.
    - A second confirm runs edit_ppt. The turn names the prior deck file and inlines its extracted text (`第2页\n总结\n• 下一步`).
    - The second artifact has `source_artifact_ref` = the first, and its download has the edited slides.
    - The first deck is still downloadable and unchanged.
    - The Home is untouched: no Beebou model call, no Beebou or `user` inputs, no pushed notice.
  - `test_a_replayed_deck_turn_reuses_its_task_and_document` (RB-S9).
  - `test_an_unusable_deck_is_final` and `test_an_unreadable_prior_deck_is_final_and_admits_nothing` (RB-S10: missing deck and tampered receipt, with no task admitted).
- Related suites: report-goals, `test_hive_host_bee_store`, `test_hive_create_bee_contract`, `test_hive_document_bytes`, `test_office_documents` and `test_hive_worker_repository`. **95 passed.**
- On a local merge with current main `3962075b` (includes #1655 and #1597): report-goals, Host Bee store, create_bee contract and repository give **73 passed**, and the architecture scanner reports **0 findings**.
- Broad run with `-n 8`: all agent_bridge tests plus hive-runtime, bee-artifacts, hive-worker and report-goals. Result: 5717 passed, 373 failed, 21 errors. The same 63 failing files, rerun on unmodified base `1e194a86` in the same venv, fail identically. These are local-environment failures (pytest selection, developer setup, credentials, workspace open, and others). The one failure not seen on base, `test_workswarm_context_consumer::test_many_deltas_do_not_block_original_response_reader`, passes 3 of 3 runs serially: a flake under parallel load.
